definition_zh: 基础的；奠基性的；根本的
definition_en: serving as the base on which something else is built or understood
core_image: 石匠把第一块方石放进坑里，后面的墙都从它起线
scene: 这里指「基础的」。 The course covers foundational concepts before moving to applied work.
sceneCN: 这里 foundational 是「基础的」（第 1 个义项：作为后续学习的前提）；句意：这门课先讲基础概念，再转向应用。图中可辨识物件：基石、水平仪、图纸、砖块。

pos.zh: 基础的；奠基性的；根本的

senses.title: The base for later learning
senses.titleCN: 基础的：后面内容都从这儿起
senses.definition: forming the basic knowledge or skills that later work depends on
senses.definitionCN: 构成后续工作所依赖的基础知识或技能的
senses.example: Foundational reading skills predict success in every other subject.
senses.exampleCN: 基础阅读能力可以预测其他所有学科的成功。
senses.why: fundus means 'bottom'. Foundational marks what sits at the bottom of a structure, holding everything above it.
senses.whyCN: fundus 意为“底部”。foundational 标记位于结构底部、托住上方一切的东西。

senses.title: Serving as a foundation
senses.definition: acting as the first established part on which a system or institution is erected
senses.definitionCN: 作为建立某个体系或制度的第一部分的
senses.example: The 1789 report is a foundational document of the public school system.
senses.exampleCN: 1789 年的那份报告是公立学校体系的奠基性文件。
senses.why: The first stone determines the line of every later stone. A foundational document does the same for an institution.
senses.whyCN: 第一块石头决定了后面每块石头的走向。一份奠基性文件对一个制度也是如此。

senses.title: Fundamental to a theory
senses.titleCN: 根本的：理论离不开的假设
senses.definition: being one of the assumptions or principles without which a theory cannot stand
senses.definitionCN: 作为理论不可或缺的假设或原则之一的
senses.example: The foundational assumption of the model is that preferences do not change.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型的基本假设是偏好不变。
senses.why: A theory rests on a few unproved commitments. Foundational names them without calling them true, only load-bearing.
senses.whyCN: 理论建立在少数未经证明的承诺上。foundational 命名它们，但不说它们为真，只说它们承重。

senses.title: Introductory in teaching
senses.definition: describing a course or lesson that teaches the first layer of a subject
senses.definitionCN: 指教授某学科第一层内容的课程或课
senses.example: The foundational course has no prerequisites.
senses.exampleCN: 这门入门课程没有先修要求。
senses.why: In a curriculum the foundation is what comes first in time as well as in depth. The word marks order and dependence at once.
senses.whyCN: 在课程体系中，基础既在深度上、也在时间上排在最前。这个词同时标记顺序与依赖关系。

senses.title: Basic science
senses.titleCN: 基础研究的：不急着应用
senses.definition: relating to research aimed at understanding basics rather than solving an immediate problem
senses.definitionCN: 指以理解基本原理为目标、而非解决眼前问题的研究
senses.example: Foundational research on cell membranes later produced a whole class of drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 关于细胞膜的基础研究后来催生了一整类药物。
senses.why: The foundation is laid below the visible building. Basic research is valued for what it will support, not for what it sells now.
senses.whyCN: 地基铺在可见建筑之下。基础研究的价值在于它将支撑什么，而不在于它现在卖什么。

senses.title: The bottom layer of a system
senses.titleCN: 底层的：整个系统压在上面
senses.definition: describing the lowest layer of a technical system that all other layers rely on
senses.definitionCN: 指技术系统中最底层、其他各层都依赖的那一层
senses.example: The foundational layer of the software handles memory and timing.
senses.exampleCN: 这个软件的底层负责内存与计时。
senses.why: Computing borrows the building image: the base layer must be stable before anything can be stacked on it.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了建筑意象：底层必须稳定，上面才堆得起来。

senses.title: Founding or establishing
senses.definition: relating to the act of founding an institution or movement
senses.definitionCN: 与创立某个机构或运动的行为有关的
senses.example: The foundational meeting elected a chair and wrote three rules.
senses.exampleCN: 创立会议选出了主席，并写下三条规则。
senses.why: This sense is close to the verb found: what is foundational is what was laid down at the beginning and still shapes the thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项接近动词 found：foundational 的东西就是开头立下、至今仍在塑造该事物的东西。

senses.title: Structurally load-bearing
senses.definition: so basic that removing it would bring the whole structure down
senses.definitionCN: 基础到抽掉它整个结构就会倒塌的
senses.example: Trust is foundational to the team; without it the rules do not work.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是团队的基础；没有它，规则就不起作用。
senses.why: The test of a foundation is removal. If taking it away collapses the rest, the word applies.
senses.whyCN: 检验地基的办法是抽掉它。若拿走它其余部分就塌，这个词就用得上。

intro.en: Foundational is foundation plus -al. Foundation comes from Latin fundatio, from fundare 'to lay a base', from fundus 'bottom'. The root pictures the bottom of a structure.
intro.cn: foundational 是 foundation 加 -al。foundation 来自拉丁 fundatio，出自 fundare“打地基”，而 fundare 又源自 fundus“底部”。词根描绘的是结构的底。

items.en: fundus meant 'bottom, base', and also 'a piece of land', because land is the bottom on which things stand. English fund, in the money sense, comes from the same word.
items.cn: fundus 意为“底部、基底”，也指“一块土地”，因为土地是万物立足之底。英语中表示资金的 fund 也来自同一个词。

items.en: fundare 'to lay a bottom, to found' turns the noun into a verb. It was used for founding cities and for laying the base of a building.
items.cn: fundare“铺底、奠基”把名词变成动词。它既用于建城，也用于给建筑打地基。

items.en: fundatio names the act of founding. English takes it as foundation, which means both the act of founding and the base that results.
items.cn: fundatio 命名奠基行为。英语借作 foundation，既指创立行为，也指由此形成的基础。

items.en: fundamentum is a parallel noun from the same verb, giving English fundamental. So foundation and fundamental are siblings, both from fundus, not one derived from the other.
items.cn: fundamentum 是同一动词的并行名词，生出英语 fundamental。因此 foundation 与 fundamental 是同胞，都来自 fundus，并非一个派生自另一个。

items.en: Foundational adds -al, from Latin -alis, to foundation. The adjective is relatively modern and became common in education and research policy in the 20th century.
items.cn: foundational 在 foundation 后加 -al（来自拉丁 -alis）。这个形容词相对晚出，20 世纪在教育与研究政策中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fund- root but splits between bottom and performance; the near-meaning group all describe something prior and load-bearing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fund- 词根，但在“底部”与“运作”之间分流；近义组都描述在先且承重之物。

entries.definition: forming the base or essence. It comes from fundamentum, a parallel noun to foundation, so the two are siblings rather than parent and child.
entries.definitionCN: 根本的；基本的。它来自 fundamentum，与 foundation 是并行名词，因此二者是同胞而非父子。

entries.definition: the base of a building or the act of founding. It is the thing; foundational is the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 地基；创立行为。它是名词；foundational 是形容词。

entries.definition: one who founds, or a ship that sinks. Both senses trace to fundus: one who lays the bottom, and one who goes to the bottom.
entries.definitionCN: 创始人；沉没的船。两个义项都可追溯到 fundus：一个铺底的人，一个沉到底的东西。

entries.definition: forming the simplest or lowest level. It is plainer and less structural than foundational.
entries.definitionCN: 构成最简单或最低层的。它比 foundational 更朴素，结构意味更弱。

entries.definition: concerned with first principles or simple parts. It often refers to early schooling.
entries.definitionCN: 关于基本原理或简单部分的。它常指早期教育。

entries.definition: situated below and often hidden, but causing what is seen. It stresses hidden depth rather than load-bearing.
entries.definitionCN: 位于下方、常不可见，却造成可见现象。它强调隐藏深度，而非承重。

entries.definition: limited to basic principles, often in an incomplete way. It can sound critical, unlike foundational.
entries.definitionCN: 仅限于基本原理，常带不完整之意。它可能带批评色彩，而 foundational 不带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fundus 'bottom' gives foundation: foundational marks what sits at the bottom and holds the rest up.
normal.cn: fundus“底部”生出 foundation：foundational 标记位于底部、托住其余部分的东西。

normal.en: foundation and fundamental are siblings from fundus and fundamentum, not one from the other.
normal.cn: foundation 与 fundamental 是来自 fundus 与 fundamentum 的同胞，并非一个派生自另一个。

normal.en: foundational concept, foundational research and foundational course are the three standard collocations.
normal.cn: foundational concept、foundational research、foundational course 是三个标准搭配。

normal.en: The removal test is the quickest check: take it away and see whether the rest collapses.
normal.cn: 抽掉检验是最快的判断法：拿走它，看其余部分是否倒塌。

normal.en: Do not confuse foundation with function: fundus is bottom, fungi is perform, and the two roots are unrelated.
normal.cn: 别把 foundation 与 function 混淆：fundus 是底部，fungi 是执行，两个词根无关。

abstract.en: Think of the first stone laid in a trench, with every later course lined up from it.
abstract.cn: 想象沟槽里放下的第一块石头，后面每一层都从它起线。

abstract.en: Think of a tree's roots underground, invisible but holding the trunk upright.
abstract.cn: 想象树根在地下，看不见，却让树干立着。

abstract.en: Think of a table with one leg removed: the whole thing falls, and that leg was foundational.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被抽掉一条腿：整张桌子倒下，那条腿就是基础的。

examples.en: The first chapter lays the foundational vocabulary for the rest of the book.
examples.cn: 第一章为全书铺设基础词汇。

examples.en: Foundational research rarely produces a product within five years.
examples.cn: 基础研究很少在五年内产出产品。

examples.en: The foundational assumption was never tested, only inherited.
examples.cn: 那个基本假设从未被检验，只是被继承下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “放（found）第一块石头”——打地基时先放第一块，后面全压在它上面 → foundational 基础的

root: 拉丁 fundus“底部、基底” → fundare“打地基” → fundatio“奠基” → 英语 foundation + -al；与 fundamental 同出 fundus 但为并行名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one test: remove it, and the structure above loses its line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个检验：抽掉它，上面的结构就失去基准线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the first stone laid in a trench.
core.cn: 核心意象：沟槽里放下的第一块石头。

branches.en: LEARNING: basic skills and introductory courses are foundations in depth and in time.
branches.cn: 学习：基础技能与入门课程，是深度与时间两个意义上的地基。

branches.en: FOUNDING: a foundational document and a founding meeting both lay down what later institutions repeat.
branches.cn: 创立：奠基性文件与创立会议，都立下后来机构反复遵循的东西。

branches.en: LOAD: an assumption and a load-bearing element are both tested by removal rather than by argument.
branches.cn: 承重：假设与承重构件，都靠“抽掉”来检验，而不是靠辩论。

branches.en: RESEARCH: basic science is valued for what it will support, not for what it sells now.
branches.cn: 研究：基础研究的价值在于它将支撑什么，而不在于它现在卖什么。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: the lowest software layer must be stable before anything can be stacked on it.
branches.cn: 系统：软件最底层必须稳定，上面才堆得起来。

intro.en: Foundational is foundation plus -al. The fund- stem means 'bottom', -atio makes an action noun and -al makes the relational adjective.
intro.cn: foundational 是 foundation 加 -al。fund- 词干意为“底部”，-atio 构成动作名词，-al 构成关系形容词。

latinIntro.en: The family grows from fundus 'bottom' through fundare 'lay a base' and fundatio 'founding'. English relatives include found, founder, foundation and fundamental.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 fundus“底部”经 fundare“打地基”与 fundatio“奠基”生长。英语同族词包括 found、founder、foundation、fundamental。

items.meaning: the act of founding; the base
items.meaningCN: 创立；地基（-tio 动作名词）
items.example: The foundation was poured in June.

items.meaningCN: 基础的；奠基性的（-al 关系形容词）
items.example: These are foundational questions.

items.meaning: to establish; to lay a base
items.example: The school was founded in 1902.
The founder left the city a library.
items.exampleCN: 创始人给这座城市留下了一座图书馆。

items.meaningCN: 根本的（fundamentum + -al，与 foundation 同胞）
items.example: The right to speak is fundamental.
The two plans differ fundamentally.

items.meaning: money set aside as a base; to provide money
items.meaningCN: 基金；资助（fundus“底、土地”，金融义另立）
items.example: The fund pays for rural clinics.
items.exampleCN: 该基金支付乡村诊所的费用。

items.meaningCN: 深刻的（pro- + fundus“底”，同一词根）
items.example: The book had a profound effect on her.

latinEntries.meaning: bottom, base; a piece of land
to lay a base, to found

latinEntries.meaningCN: 基础；地基（fundamental 的直接来源）

definition_zh: 尽管；不顾（后接名词或动名词，不直接接从句）
definition_en: despite; used before a noun or gerund to concede an obstacle that did not stop something
core_image: 一个人顶着逆风把推车推上斜坡，车轮仍向前
scene: 风力很大，送货员仍把推车推上斜坡。 The delivery went ahead in spite of the strong wind.
sceneCN: 这里取「尽管」（第 1 个义项：后接名词，承认阻碍但结果未变）；句意为尽管风大，送货仍照常进行。

pos.zh: 介词短语：尽管、不顾（后接名词或动名词）

collocations.phrase: in spite of the fact that

forms.label: 事实从句
forms.form: in spite of the fact that

senses.title: Conceding an obstacle named by a noun
senses.definition: used before a noun to admit that an obstacle existed while saying the result was unchanged
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，承认阻碍存在，同时说明结果未变
senses.example: The delivery went ahead in spite of the strong wind.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管风很大，送货仍照常进行。
senses.why: The phrase admits the obstacle first and denies its effect second, which is the opposite order from a cause phrase.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语先承认阻碍，再否认其效果，与因果短语的顺序正好相反。

senses.title: Conceding an activity
senses.definition: used before an -ing form when the obstacle is an activity or a process
senses.definitionCN: 当阻碍是活动或过程时，用在动名词之前
senses.example: She finished the report in spite of feeling unwell.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管身体不适，她还是完成了报告。
senses.why: A prepositional phrase cannot take a bare verb, so the activity appears as a gerund.
senses.whyCN: 介词短语不能接光秃秃的动词，所以活动以动名词出现。

senses.title: Conceding a full statement
senses.titleCN: 尽管事实是：后接事实从句
senses.definition: used before the fact that when the obstacle is a whole statement
senses.definitionCN: 当阻碍是完整命题时，用在「事实是」之前
senses.example: The plan succeeded in spite of the fact that funding was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管经费被削减，计划还是成功了。
senses.why: The fact that frame is the standard route to a clause after this prepositional phrase.
senses.whyCN: 「事实是」框架是这一介词短语后接从句的标准通道。

senses.title: The front-position concession
senses.definition: placed at the start of a sentence to set up the concession before the main claim
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，在主句之前先摆出让步
senses.example: In spite of the delay, the goods arrived intact.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管延误，货物完好送达。
senses.why: Fronting the concession makes the main clause read as a triumph over the obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 把让步前置，主句便读作对阻碍的胜利。

senses.title: The trailing concession
senses.definition: placed after the main clause to add the obstacle as an afterthought
senses.definitionCN: 放在主句之后，把阻碍作为补充
senses.example: The team finished on time, in spite of every setback.
senses.exampleCN: 团队按时完成，尽管遭遇了种种挫折。
senses.why: Trailing position keeps the achievement first and lets the obstacle follow as a qualification.
senses.whyCN: 后置把成绩放在前面，让阻碍随后作为限定。

senses.title: The boundary against a shorter synonym
senses.titleCN: 与更短同义介词的边界
senses.definition: it carries the same meaning as a shorter synonym but is slightly heavier and more conversational
senses.definitionCN: 它与更短的同义介词意义相同，但语气略重、更口语
senses.example: In spite of the cost, the plan was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管成本高，计划仍获批准。
senses.why: The shorter synonym is more formal and cannot take the fact frame as naturally, so the choice is a matter of weight and idiom.
senses.whyCN: 更短的同义词更正式，接事实框架也不如它自然，因此选择取决于分量与习惯。

senses.title: The fixed phrase of involuntary action
senses.definition: in the fixed pattern in spite of oneself, used when a reaction happens against one's will
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法「不由自主」中，表示反应违背本人意愿而发生
senses.example: She laughed in spite of herself.
senses.exampleCN: 她不由自主地笑了。
senses.why: Here spite turns inward: the person's own will is the obstacle that the reaction overrides.
senses.whyCN: 此处「恶意」转向自身：本人的意愿成了被反应压过的阻碍。

senses.title: The grammatical boundary against a conjunction
senses.titleCN: 语法边界：不能直接接从句
senses.definition: unlike a concessive conjunction, it cannot be followed directly by a clause
senses.definitionCN: 与让步连词不同，它后面不能直接跟从句
senses.example: In spite of the rain, the match continued.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管下雨，比赛仍继续。
senses.why: This is the grammar that separates it from although: a preposition needs a noun, while a conjunction takes a clause.
senses.whyCN: 这正是它与让步连词的分界：介词要名词，连词接从句。

intro.en: Spite comes from Middle English despite, from Old French despit, from Latin despicere, to look down on, itself de-, down, and specere, to look. The Latin line is clear; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: spite 来自中古英语 despite，经古法语 despit，出自拉丁语 despicere「俯视、轻视」，由 de-「向下」与 specere「看」构成。拉丁语线索清楚，短语属近代。

items.en: Specere, to look, is also the root of spectacle and specimen.
items.cn: specere 意为「看」，也是 spectacle 与 specimen 的词根。

items.en: Despicere meant to look down on, hence to scorn.
items.cn: despicere 意为俯视，由此引申为轻视。

items.en: Old French despit meant contempt or vexation, and English took it as despite.
items.cn: 古法语 despit 意为轻蔑或恼怒，英语借入作 despite。

items.en: English kept despite as a preposition of concession and spite as a noun of malice.
items.cn: 英语保留 despite 作让步介词，spite 作表恶意的名词。

items.en: The phrase with this noun and preposition settles in modern English; dates are approximate.
items.cn: 带这个名词与介词的短语在近代英语中定型，年代为约数。

note.en: The first group also concedes an obstacle but differs in grammar or in the direction of the concession; the second group holds conjunctions and adverbs of concession.
note.cn: 第一组同样承认阻碍，但语法或让步方向不同；第二组是表让步的连词与副词。

entries.definition: It is the shorter synonym and is commoner in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 它是更短的同义词，在正式文字中更常见。

entries.definition: A formal legal preposition meaning in spite of.
entries.definitionCN: 正式法律介词，意为尽管。

entries.definition: It denies that the factor matters at all, while this phrase admits it exists.
entries.definitionCN: 它否认因素有任何分量，而本短语承认其存在。

entries.definition: It concedes a fact and often hints that the concession is grudging.
entries.definitionCN: 承认事实，常暗示让步并不情愿。

entries.definition: It takes a full clause, which a preposition cannot do.
entries.definitionCN: 它接完整从句，介词做不到。

entries.definition: It concedes the previous point in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在口语中承认上一点。

entries.definition: It marks the main clause as surviving a stated obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 标记主句在所述阻碍下仍成立。

entries.definition: It concedes a possible condition rather than an existing fact.
entries.definitionCN: 它承认可能条件，而非既存事实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real looking-down root, the real concession grammar and the real fixed phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实「俯视」词根、真实让步语法与真实固定说法。

normal.en: The root is looking down on something, so the phrase began as a picture of scorn overcome.
normal.cn: 词根是俯视某物，所以短语最初是「轻蔑被克服」的画面。

normal.en: It takes a noun or a gerund, never a clause.
normal.cn: 它接名词或动名词，从不接从句。

normal.en: A full statement needs the fact that frame.
normal.cn: 完整命题需要「事实是」框架。

normal.en: At the front it sets up a triumph; at the end it adds a qualification.
normal.cn: 放句首搭起胜利，放句末补上限定。

normal.en: In spite of oneself turns the scorn inward, against one's own will.
normal.cn: 「不由自主」把轻蔑转向内部，违背本人意愿。

abstract.en: Like a cart pushed up a slope against a strong headwind, still reaching the top.
abstract.cn: 像推车顶着强逆风上坡，仍然到达坡顶。

abstract.en: Like a letter delivered in the rain with the ink still dry.
abstract.cn: 像雨中送到的信，字迹仍然干燥。

abstract.en: Like a laugh that escapes before the person decides to laugh.
abstract.cn: 像笑意在人决定之前就先跑出来。

examples.cn: 尽管下雨，比赛仍继续。

examples.en: In spite of the cost, the committee approved the plan.
examples.cn: 尽管成本高，委员会仍批准了计划。

examples.en: She finished the work in spite of feeling ill.

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split by complement and position: a noun, a gerund, a fact clause, front and trailing concessions, the boundary against a shorter synonym, the fixed phrase of involuntary action, and the grammar boundary against a conjunction.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项按搭配与位置区分：名词、动名词、事实从句、句首与句末让步、与更短同义词的边界、「不由自主」固定说法、与连词的语法边界。

core.cn: 核心意象：推车顶着强逆风上坡，仍然到达坡顶。

branches.en: THE OBSTACLE: a noun or an activity is admitted before the result is asserted.
branches.cn: 阻碍：先承认名词或活动，再断言结果。

branches.cn: 命题：完整从句需要事实框架。

branches.cn: 位置：前置搭起胜利，后置补上限定。

branches.cn: 分量：较长短语比同义词更重、更口语。

branches.en: THE INWARD AND THE GRAMMAR: involuntary action turns scorn inward, and the phrase takes no clause directly.
branches.cn: 向内与语法：不由自主把轻蔑转向内部，且短语不直接接从句。

intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁语「轻蔑」名词与英语介词结合；「俯视」词根是核心。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词源是 despicere「俯视」与 specere「看」。

definition_zh: 疏远；疏离感；（哲学）异化；（法律）转让
definition_en: the state of feeling isolated from people, work or society; in social theory, estrangement from your own labour; in law, the transfer of property
core_image: 站在人群里却觉得隔着一层玻璃
scene: 搬进新城市半年，他每天上班打卡，却谁也不认识。 Alienation grew quietly behind his polite smile.
sceneCN: 这里 alienation 是「疏离感」（第 1 个义项：与周围人或环境失去联系的心理状态）；句意为疏离感在他礼貌的微笑背后悄悄滋长。核心画面是站在人群里却觉得隔着一层玻璃。

forms.label: 不可数名词，无复数形式

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ion 的动词，义为「使疏远；转让」
过去分词作形容词，义为「感到被疏远的」

senses.title: The feeling of being cut off
senses.definition: the state of feeling isolated from the people, work or society around you, as though a wall stood between you and them
senses.definitionCN: 感到与周围的人、工作或社会隔绝的状态，仿佛彼此之间立着一道墙
senses.example: Long shifts and empty weekends deepened his alienation.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的班次与空荡的周末加深了他的疏离感。
senses.why: Alien means other, and -ation names a state, so alienation is the state of having become other: you are among people yet no longer of them.
senses.whyCN: alien 意为「他者」，-ation 表示状态，所以 alienation 就是「已成为他者」的状态：你在人群之中，却不再属于他们。

senses.title: Loss of control over your own work
senses.definition: in social theory, the condition in which workers lose control over what they make and feel estranged from their own labour
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论中，劳动者失去对自己产品的控制、并与自身劳动相疏离的状态
senses.example: Marx described alienation as the worker lost in the product.
senses.exampleCN: 马克思把异化描述为劳动者在自己的产品中失落。
senses.why: This sense narrows the general wall to one specific place: the workshop, where what you build no longer feels like yours.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把那堵普遍的墙收窄到一个具体场所：车间，你造出来的东西不再感觉属于你。

senses.title: The legal transfer of property
senses.definition: in law, the act of transferring ownership of property to another person, the oldest sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 法律上把财产所有权转移给他人的行为，是该词最古老的用法
senses.example: The deed records the alienation of the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这份契据记录了家族农场的转让。
senses.why: Here the word stays literal: making a thing alien means making it the property of someone else, which is precisely what a transfer does.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词保持字面义：让某物变成 alien「别人的」，正是转让所做的事。

intro.en: Alienation is the noun of alienate: Latin alienus, belonging to another, plus the process suffix -ation, naming the state of having been made other.
intro.cn: alienation 是 alienate 的名词形式：拉丁语 alienus「属于别人的」加过程后缀 -ation，表示「已被变成他者」的状态。

items.en: Latin alius meant other, the root of alias, alibi and alter.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alius 意为「其他」，是 alias、alibi 与 alter 的词根。

items.en: Alienus meant belonging to another, and so foreign, strange or unrelated.
items.cn: alienus 意为「属于别人的」，因此引申为外国的、陌生的、无关的。

items.en: The noun alienatio named a transfer of ownership in Roman law, and also a loss of reason or affection.
items.cn: 名词 alienatio 在罗马法中指所有权转让，也指理智或感情的丧失。

items.en: Old French alienation kept the legal sense, and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 alienation 保留法律义，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: Philosophy and sociology widened the word in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries to name estrangement from work and society.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，哲学与社会学拓宽该词，用以指与劳动和社会的疏离。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the ali- family of otherness; the near-meaning group lists other words for feeling cut off.
note.cn: 形近组保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词族；近义组列出其他表示「感到隔绝」的词。

entries.definitionCN: 使某人变得冷淡或敌对。

entries.definition: Belonging to another place or person.
entries.definitionCN: 属于别处或别人的。

entries.definition: Feeling isolated and unwanted.
entries.definitionCN: 感到孤立、不被接纳的。

entries.definition: A change made to something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物所做的改动。

entries.definition: The state of being alone and separated.

entries.definition: The loss of affection between people.
entries.definitionCN: 人与人之间感情的丧失。

entries.definition: Sadness at being alone.
entries.definitionCN: 因独处而产生的难过。

entries.definition: A break in a link or relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 联系或关系的中断。

normalIntro.en: Alienation is alienate plus -ion: the state produced when someone is made alien.
normalIntro.cn: alienation 就是 alienate 加 -ion：把某人变成外人之后产生的那种状态。

normal.en: Alienate is the verb, alienation the result: one pushes, the other is the distance left.
normal.cn: alienate 是动词，alienation 是结果：一个是推，一个是推完后留下的距离。

normal.en: Alien means other, so alienation is otherness turned into a feeling.
normal.cn: alien 意为「他者」，所以 alienation 就是「他者性」变成的一种感受。

normal.en: It is uncountable, so say a sense of alienation, not an alienation.
normal.cn: 它不可数，所以说 a sense of alienation，不说 an alienation。

normal.en: In sociology alienation from work is a fixed phrase; keep the from.
normal.cn: 社会学中 alienation from work 是固定搭配，别丢掉 from。

normal.en: In law the alienation of property simply means its transfer.
normal.cn: 法律上 the alienation of property 就是财产转让。

abstract.en: Picture standing in a crowded room behind a sheet of glass.
abstract.cn: 想象站在拥挤的房间里，面前隔着一层玻璃。

abstract.en: Imagine building a chair all day and never being allowed to sit in it.
abstract.cn: 想象整天做椅子，却从不被允许坐上去。

abstract.en: Think of your own name written on a door you can no longer open.
abstract.cn: 想象你自己的名字写在一扇你再也打不开的门上。

examples.en: Alienation often follows a long move to a new city.
examples.cn: 搬到一个新城市后，疏离感常常随之而来。

examples.en: The survey measured alienation among night-shift workers.
examples.cn: 这项调查测量了夜班工人的疏离感。

examples.en: Any alienation of the land needs the consent of both heirs.
examples.cn: 这块土地的任何转让都需两位继承人同意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「诶里诶内申」——诶里（alien）是外人，诶内申（ation）是状态：变成外人的那种状态，就是疏离、异化。

root: 拉丁语 alius「其他」派生出 alienus「属于别人的」，加动词后缀构成 alienare「转让、使疏远」，其名词 alienatio 经古法语 alienation 进入英语，字面即「被变成他者的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses describe the same crossing: a person becomes other to their community, a worker becomes other to their product, and a property becomes other to its owner.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项描述的是同一次跨越：人对自己的社群成为他者，劳动者对自己的产品成为他者，财产对原主成为他者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glass wall between you and what was yours
core.cn: 核心意象：你与原本属于你的一切之间隔着一层玻璃

branches.en: A polite smile hiding no real contact.
branches.cn: 礼貌的微笑背后没有真正的接触。

branches.en: A new city where nobody knows your name.
branches.cn: 一座没人知道你名字的新城市。

branches.en: A worker who never owns what they build.
branches.cn: 从不拥有自己产品的劳动者。

branches.en: A deed moving land to another name.
branches.cn: 把土地转到别人名下的契据。

branches.en: All three make what was yours into the property of another.
branches.cn: 三者都把原本属于你的变成别人的。

intro.en: Alienation keeps the ali- root of otherness, the verb suffix -ate and the result suffix -ion, so the whole history is visible in the spelling.
intro.cn: alienation 保留表示「他者」的 ali- 词根、动词后缀 -ate 与结果后缀 -ion，整段历史都写在拼写里。

latinIntro.en: Latin alius gave alienus, alienare and the noun alienatio, which French passed to English with both senses intact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alius 派生出 alienus、alienare 与名词 alienatio，法语把它传给英语时两义都完好保留。

definition_zh: 太阳系；太阳与受其引力束缚的全部天体及物质
definition_en: the sun together with all the bodies bound to it by gravity, including the planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets
core_image: 一圈圈同心椭圆围绕中央一颗发亮的黄球，内侧撒着碎石，外侧是带环的巨行星与冰屑带
scene: 博物馆大厅的地板上画着一圈圈同心轨道，中央是一颗发亮的黄球，最外圈散着冰屑。 On the museum floor, rings of light trace the solar system around a glowing yellow sun.
sceneCN: 这里 solar system 指「太阳与受其引力束缚的全部天体」（第 1 个义项：以引力范围定义的天文学整体）；句意为地板上的同心光环围绕发亮的黄色太阳，勾出太阳系。图中可辨识物件：地板、同心轨道、黄球、冰屑、参观者的鞋尖。

pos.zh: 太阳系（可数，通常带定冠词 the；复数指别的恒星系统）

collocations.phrase: the formation of the solar system
a model of the solar system

senses.title: The sun and everything bound to it
senses.titleCN: 太阳与受其引力束缚的一切
senses.definition: the sun and all the matter held in orbit around it by its gravity
senses.definitionCN: 太阳以及被其引力维持在轨道上的一切物质
senses.example: On the museum floor, rings of light trace the solar system around a glowing yellow sun.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆地板上，一圈圈光环围绕发亮的黄色太阳，勾出太阳系。
senses.why: the phrase defines the system by its centre: whatever the sun holds becomes part of it, so the boundary is gravitational rather than fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语以中心定义系统：凡被太阳维系者都属其中，因此边界是引力边界而非固定界线。

senses.title: The eight planets and their neighbourhood
senses.titleCN: 八大行星及其中近邻区域
senses.definition: the region containing the eight planets, their moons and the belts of small bodies between and beyond them
senses.definitionCN: 包含八大行星、它们的卫星，以及其间与外侧小天体带的区域
senses.example: The four inner planets of the solar system are rocky and fairly small.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系的四颗内行星由岩石构成，体积较小。
senses.why: the planets are the largest bound bodies, so the phrase often means their arrangement, even though the system contains far more small debris.
senses.whyCN: 行星是最大的被束缚天体，因此这个短语常指它们的布局，尽管系统中还有远多得多的小碎块。

senses.title: Classes of bodies within it
senses.definition: used to group the objects involved: planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets and dust
senses.definitionCN: 用于归类其中的天体：行星、矮行星、卫星、小行星、彗星与尘埃
senses.example: Comets carry frozen material from the outer solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星带着来自太阳系外层的冻结物质。
senses.why: a system is also a set of categories, so textbooks use the phrase as a container for every object class it holds.
senses.whyCN: 系统同时也是一组类别，因此教材用这个短语来容纳其中的每一个天体类别。

senses.title: Its outer boundary
senses.titleCN: 太阳系边界：日球层与奥尔特云
senses.definition: the outer limits marked by the solar wind's bubble and the distant shell of icy bodies
senses.definitionCN: 由太阳风气泡与远处冰质天体壳层标出的外缘
senses.example: Voyager crossed the heliopause, the edge of the solar system's magnetic bubble.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行者号越过了日球层顶，即太阳系磁泡的边缘。
senses.why: since gravity binds bodies far beyond the planets, the phrase needed a practical edge, and the wind's bubble supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 由于引力束缚的天体远在行星之外，这个短语需要一个实用边界，而太阳风气泡提供了它。

senses.title: How it formed
senses.definition: the system as a product of a collapsing cloud of gas and dust about four and a half billion years ago
senses.definitionCN: 约四十五亿年前一团气体与尘埃云坍缩的产物
senses.example: The solar system formed from a disk of dust that later gathered into planets.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系由一片后来聚成行星的尘埃盘形成。
senses.why: the objects share an age and a composition, so the phrase naturally names a common history rather than only a present arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 这些天体共享同一年龄与成分，因此这个短语自然指一段共同历史，而不只是当下的布局。

senses.title: Other systems by analogy
senses.titleCN: 类比：其他恒星的行星系统
senses.definition: used in the plural for systems of planets around other stars, measured against ours
senses.definitionCN: 用复数指其他恒星周围的行星系统，并以我们的系统为参照
senses.example: Astronomers now compare solar systems around distant stars with our own.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家如今把远处恒星周围的行星系统与我们的系统相比较。
senses.why: once other planetary systems were found, the familiar phrase became a template, and the plural marks the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 当其他行星系统被发现后，这个熟悉的短语成了模板，复数形式标记的正是这种比较。

senses.title: A person's private centre
senses.titleCN: 比喻：以某人为中心的圈子
senses.definition: figuratively, the circle of people and interests that revolve around one person
senses.definitionCN: 比喻一个人周围旋转的人与事的圈子
senses.example: His office was a small solar system of assistants and messengers.
senses.exampleCN: 他的办公室是一个由助理与信使构成的小小太阳系。
senses.why: the image of bodies circling a centre transfers easily to social life, where one person is the centre others orbit.
senses.whyCN: 天体绕中心的意象很容易转到社交生活：一个人成为中心，别人绕着他转。

senses.title: A model or orrery
senses.definition: a physical or digital model that shows the planets moving around the sun
senses.definitionCN: 展示行星绕太阳运动的实体或数字模型
senses.example: The classroom solar system had brass arms and a lamp for the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 教室里的太阳系模型有黄铜臂，用一盏灯代表太阳。
senses.why: because the real system is too large to see at once, the phrase is also used for the model that stands in for it.
senses.whyCN: 真实的系统大到无法一次看见，因此这个短语也用于替代它的模型。

intro.en: Solar system joins solar, from Latin solaris and sol 'sun', to system, from Greek systema 'an organised whole'. The English phrase is modern, tied to the Copernican view. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solar system 由 solar 与 system 组合：前者来自拉丁 solaris、sol「太阳」，后者来自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」。这一英语短语属近代说法，与哥白尼体系相关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin sol, solis meant 'sun'. Its older Indo-European shape is reconstructed, not recorded, and Greek helios 'sun' is a related but separate form.
items.cn: 拉丁 sol、solis 意为「太阳」。其更早的印欧语形态是重构的，并无记录；希腊 helios「太阳」是相关而独立的形态。

items.en: Solaris 'of the sun' supplied the adjective; English solar came through French and Latin rather than directly from the noun.
items.cn: solaris「太阳的」提供了形容词；英语 solar 经法语与拉丁语而来，并非直接取自名词。

items.en: Greek systema meant 'a whole put together', built on syn- 'together' and histanai 'to set up, stand'.
items.cn: 希腊 systema 意为「组合起来的整体」，由 syn-「一起」与 histanai「安置、站立」构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed systema from Greek, and European languages took it as the ordinary word for an ordered set of parts.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊借入 systema，欧洲各语言又把它作为「有序部件集合」的常用词。

items.en: Once the sun rather than the earth was placed at the centre, the phrase solar system became the natural label for the arrangement.
items.cn: 一旦太阳而非地球被置于中心，solar system 便成为描述这一布局的当然名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated, and the reconstructed Indo-European form for 'sun' is a hypothesis rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切短语最早的英语用例没有可靠年代；表示「太阳」的印欧语重构形式属于假说，并非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built from the same two words or their relatives; group two holds larger or neighbouring astronomical units.
note.cn: 第一组是由这两个词或其同族构成的短语；第二组是更大或相邻的天文单位。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of the sun'; on its own it describes anything sun-related, from panels to storms.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「太阳的」的形容词；单独使用时描述任何与太阳有关的事物，从电池板到风暴。

entries.definition: The general noun for an organised set of parts; outside astronomy it names transport, legal or computer systems.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指有序部件集合的名词；在天文学之外，它指交通、法律或计算机系统。

entries.definition: A system of planets and smaller bodies around a star; it names the planets' side of the arrangement rather than the sun.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕恒星的行星与小天体系统；它强调的是行星一侧，而非太阳。

entries.definition: A small group of stars bound by gravity, such as a binary; the phrase does not require planets at all.
entries.definitionCN: 受引力束缚的小群恒星，如双星；这个短语完全不必有行星。

entries.definition: A system of hundreds of billions of stars; the solar system is one small part of the Milky Way.
entries.definitionCN: 包含数千亿颗恒星的系统；太阳系只是银河系的一小部分。

entries.definition: All matter and space taken together; it contains countless galaxies, so it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 一切物质与空间的总和；它包含无数星系，因此不是同义词。

entries.definition: The region dominated by the solar wind; it is often treated as the system's practical outer edge.
entries.definitionCN: 由太阳风主导的区域；常被视为太阳系的实用外缘。

entries.definition: The universe seen as an ordered whole, from Greek kosmos; a much wider word than the solar system.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为有序整体的宇宙，来自希腊 kosmos；比太阳系宽泛得多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real astronomy and real morphemes, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词、真实的天文学与真实语素，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sol 'sun' + -ar, and systema 'organised whole': the sun's organised whole.
normal.cn: sol「太阳」+ -ar，再加 systema「有组织的整体」：太阳的有序整体。

normal.en: The phrase became standard once the sun replaced the earth at the centre.
normal.cn: 当太阳取代地球成为中心，这个短语才成为标准说法。

normal.en: Eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets all belong to it.
normal.cn: 八大行星、它们的卫星、矮行星、小行星与彗星都属于它。

normal.en: Its edge is marked by the heliopause, where the solar wind meets interstellar gas.
normal.cn: 它的边缘由日球层顶标出，那里太阳风与星际气体相遇。

normal.en: Plural solar systems compare our arrangement with planets around other stars.
normal.cn: 复数 solar systems 把我们的布局与其他恒星周围的行星相比较。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp in a dark hall with dust specks slowly circling it.
abstract.cn: 想象暗厅里一盏灯，尘埃微粒绕着它慢慢转。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree where every descendant still answers to one ancestor.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家族树，每个后代都仍听命于同一位祖先。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in still water: rings spread outward from one point.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水：一圈圈涟漪从一点向外散开。

examples.en: Jupiter holds most of the mass of the solar system outside the sun.
examples.cn: 太阳系中除太阳以外的质量，大部分集中在木星。

examples.en: The solar system's outer region is crowded with icy bodies.
examples.cn: 太阳系的外层区域挤满了冰质天体。

examples.en: A simple solar system model shows why inner planets move faster.
examples.cn: 一个简单的太阳系模型就能说明内行星为何运动更快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜了（solar）＋系统（system）」——搜罗太阳管着的一整套天体 → 太阳系

root: 拉丁 sol「太阳」+ 形容词后缀 -aris 构成 solaris，再加希腊 systema「有组织的整体」（syn-「一起」+ histanai「安置」）。英语 solar system 为近代短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the gravitational whole, narrow to the planets, widen to object classes and the boundary, then move to its origin, to other stars' systems, to a metaphor and finally to a model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从引力整体出发，收窄到行星，再扩大到天体类别与边界，随后转向它的起源、别的恒星系统、一个比喻，最后落到模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright centre with rings of debris circling it at different distances.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个发亮的中心，周围有碎石环在不同距离上绕行。

branches.en: WHOLE AND CORE: the gravitational whole is usually spoken of through its planets.
branches.cn: 整体与核心：引力整体通常通过行星来谈论。

branches.en: CATALOGUE: naming the classes turns the system into an inventory.
branches.cn: 目录：命名各类天体把这个系统变成一份清单。

branches.en: EDGE: the wind's bubble gives the whole a workable border.
branches.cn: 边缘：太阳风气泡给整体一个可用的边界。

branches.en: HISTORY AND ANALOGY: one origin, and then the same phrase applied to other stars.
branches.cn: 历史与类比：一个共同起源，随后同一短语被用于其他恒星。

branches.en: SMALL COPY: a social circle or a classroom model repeats the centre-and-orbits shape.
branches.cn: 缩小的复制：社交圈子或课堂模型重复了「中心与环绕」的形状。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin root for the sun, a Latin adjective suffix, and a Greek noun for an organised whole.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个表示太阳的拉丁词根、一个拉丁形容词后缀，以及一个表示「有序整体」的希腊名词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sol and solaris supply the sun half, and Latin systema, borrowed from Greek, supplies the whole half; the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sol 与 solaris 提供「太阳」一半，拉丁从希腊借入的 systema 提供「整体」一半；复合本身是近代英语。

items.example: The root also gives solstice and solar.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还构成 solstice 与 solar。

items.example: Solaris became English solar.
The prefix survives in system, symmetry and synthesis.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀存留在 system、symmetry 与 synthesis 中。

items.example: Greek systema became Latin systema and English system.
items.exampleCN: 希腊 systema 成为拉丁 systema 与英语 system。

items.example: Solar panels turn light into current.
items.exampleCN: 太阳能板把光变成电流。

items.example: The probe left the solar system's inner region.
items.exampleCN: 探测器离开了太阳系的内层区域。

items.example: Most known planetary systems differ from ours.
items.exampleCN: 已知的行星系统大多与我们的不同。

items.example: The heliosphere shields the planets from cosmic rays.
items.exampleCN: 日球层为行星挡住宇宙射线。

latinEntries.structure: systema, systematis (n., third declension; borrowed from Greek)

definition_zh: v. 耗尽；使枯竭；大量减少（资源、存量）
definition_en: to reduce something greatly in number or quantity, especially a supply
core_image: 水库岸边露出一圈圈旧水位线，油罐的指针一点点往零走
scene: 干旱耗尽了水库的水。 The drought depleted the reservoir.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：depleted 指耗尽；句意是干旱耗尽了水库的水。

senses.title: Use up a supply
senses.definition: to use up a supply until little is left
senses.definitionCN: 把供给用到所剩无几
senses.example: The drought depleted the reservoir.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱耗尽了水库的水。
senses.why: Old water lines showing on a dry bank.
senses.whyCN: 干涸岸边露出的一圈圈旧水位线。

senses.title: Reduce numbers
senses.definition: to reduce the number of people or things greatly
senses.definitionCN: 大幅减少人或物的数量
senses.example: Overfishing has depleted the cod stocks.
senses.exampleCN: 过度捕捞使鳕鱼资源枯竭。
senses.why: A net coming up nearly empty.
senses.whyCN: 一张几乎空着被拉上来的网。

senses.title: Weaken a body or fund
senses.definition: to drain strength, energy or money from something
senses.definitionCN: 把力气、精力或金钱从某处抽走
senses.example: The illness depleted her strength.
senses.exampleCN: 这场病耗尽了她的体力。
senses.why: A gauge needle creeping towards zero.
senses.whyCN: 一根一点点爬向零的指针。

intro.en: Deplete comes from Latin deplere, de- plus plere, to fill, from plenus, full: to empty what was full.
intro.cn: deplete 源自拉丁语 deplere，由 de- 加 plere（装满）构成，plere 来自 plenus（满的）：把满的倒空。

items.en: Plenus meant full.
items.cn: plenus 意为满的。

items.en: Plere meant to fill.
items.cn: plere 意为装满。

items.en: Deplere meant to empty out.
items.cn: deplere 意为倒空。

items.en: Deplete entered English for emptying a supply.
items.cn: 十七世纪 deplete 以耗空供给义进入英语。

items.en: It was used for draining resources and funds.
items.cn: 十九世纪用于资源与资金的耗减。

items.en: Ozone and fish stocks made it a common term.
items.cn: 臭氧与鱼类资源让它成为常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ple- filling family; the near-meaning group names other ways of emptying something.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ple-（装满）家族；近义组是其他「弄空」的说法。

entries.definition: The act of using up a supply.
entries.definitionCN: 耗减。

entries.definition: To finish, or having all parts.
entries.definitionCN: 完成；完整的。

entries.definition: Filled or well supplied with something.
entries.definitionCN: 充满的。

entries.definition: To use up completely.
entries.definitionCN: 耗尽。

entries.definition: To draw liquid or strength away.
entries.definitionCN: 排空；耗竭。

entries.definition: To make or become smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 减少。

normalIntro.en: Deplete is de- away plus ple- full: take the fullness away until the gauge reads zero.
normalIntro.cn: deplete 就是 de-（去掉）加 ple-（满）：把满拿走，直到指针读零。

normal.en: Ple- means to fill, as in complete.
normal.cn: ple- 意为装满，如 complete。

normal.en: De- means away.
normal.cn: de- 表示去掉。

normal.en: Deplete a reservoir and the banks show.
normal.cn: 耗干水库，旧岸线就露出来。

normal.en: Overfishing depletes the stock.
normal.cn: 过度捕捞使鱼群枯竭。

normal.en: Illness depletes strength.
normal.cn: 疾病耗尽体力。

abstract.en: Old water lines showing on a dry bank.
abstract.cn: 干涸岸边露出的一圈圈旧水位线。

abstract.en: A net coming up nearly empty.
abstract.cn: 一张几乎空着被拉上来的网。

abstract.en: A gauge needle creeping towards zero.
abstract.cn: 一根一点点爬向零的指针。

examples.en: The war depleted the national reserves.
examples.cn: 战争耗尽了国家储备。

examples.en: Pumping is depleting the aquifer.
examples.cn: 抽水正在耗减地下水层。

examples.en: One bad season depletes the whole fund.
examples.cn: 一个坏年景就能耗空整笔基金。

dict_mnemonic.text: deplete 谐音「弟普立特」——不如记 de（去掉）＋ plete（满，与 complete 同根 plenus）＝把满的去掉，「耗尽、枯竭」。

root: 拉丁语 plenus（满）→ plere（装满）→ de-＋plere → deplere（倒空）→ 英语 deplete

sensesIntro.en: One fullness taken away: a reservoir, a fish stock and a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一份被拿走的满：一座水库、一群鱼与一个身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: old water lines on a dry bank and a gauge needle creeping towards zero
core.cn: 核心意象：干涸岸边一圈圈旧水位线，指针一点点爬向零

branches.en: Old water lines showing on a dry bank.
branches.cn: 干涸岸边露出的一圈圈旧水位线。

branches.en: A net coming up nearly empty.

branches.en: A gauge needle creeping towards zero.
branches.cn: 一根一点点爬向零的指针。

branches.en: Both take a stock down to very little.
branches.cn: 两者都把存量降到所剩无几。

branches.en: Both leave less than what was there before.
branches.cn: 两者都让剩下的比原先少。

intro.en: Deplete is de- plus ple-; the filling root builds the full and empty families.
intro.cn: deplete 由 de- 加 ple- 构成；装满这个词根造出满与空两族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin plenus means full, plere to fill and haurire to draw out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 plenus 意为满，plere 意为装满，haurire 意为抽出。

definition_zh: 食碎屑动物；以腐屑为食的动物
definition_en: an animal that feeds on detritus, the dead and broken fragments of other organisms
core_image: 一只小虾在河底把烂叶碎片一点点送进嘴里
scene: 这里指「食碎屑动物」。 The mayfly larva is a detritivore that shreds leaf litter at the bottom of the stream.
sceneCN: 这里 detritivore 是「食碎屑动物」（第 1 个义项：以腐屑为食的动物）；句意：蜉蝣幼虫是食碎屑动物，在溪流底部把落叶撕碎取食。

pos.zh: 食碎屑动物；食腐屑生物（可数，复数 detritivores）

senses.title: An animal living on detritus
senses.definition: an animal whose main food is dead, fragmented organic matter
senses.definitionCN: 以死亡、破碎的有机物为主要食物的动物
senses.example: Earthworms are detritivores that process enormous amounts of soil.
senses.exampleCN: 蚯蚓是食碎屑动物，处理大量土壤。
senses.why: The word combines the name of the food with the -vore ending for eaters, so the diet itself defines the animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把食物的名称与表示取食者的 -vore 词尾结合，因此食性本身就定义了这种动物。

senses.title: A bottom-dwelling shredder
senses.definition: an aquatic animal that shreds and eats leaf litter and other coarse detritus on the bottom
senses.definitionCN: 在水底撕碎并取食落叶等粗大腐屑的水生动物
senses.example: Caddis larvae are detritivores that break leaves into finer particles.
senses.exampleCN: 石蛾幼虫是食碎屑动物，把叶片破碎成更细的颗粒。
senses.why: Stream ecology focuses on the mechanical act of shredding, because it converts coarse litter into food others can use.
senses.whyCN: 溪流生态学关注「撕碎」这一机械动作，因为它把粗大枯落物变成其他生物可用的食物。

senses.title: A soil worker
senses.definition: a soil animal that feeds on dead plant material and mixes it into the soil
senses.definitionCN: 取食死亡植物材料并将其混入土壤的土壤动物
senses.example: The soil detritivore population doubled after the leaf fall.
senses.exampleCN: 落叶之后，土壤食碎屑动物的数量翻了一番。
senses.why: Soil biology highlights the mixing effect: feeding on fragments is also a way of building soil structure.
senses.whyCN: 土壤生物学强调混合作用：取食碎片同时也是构建土壤结构的方式。

senses.title: A member of a feeding guild
senses.definition: an organism classified in the detritus food chain by its feeding role
senses.definitionCN: 按取食角色被归入碎屑食物链的生物
senses.example: The study grouped detritivores, grazers and predators by guild.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究按功能群把食碎屑者、刮食者与捕食者分组。
senses.why: Ecology classifies by function, so any animal that eats detritus joins the same guild regardless of taxonomy.
senses.whyCN: 生态学按功能分类，因此任何吃碎屑的动物都归入同一功能群，无论分类地位如何。

senses.title: The partner of decomposers
senses.titleCN: 与分解者分工的取食者
senses.definition: an animal that reduces particle size so microbes can complete chemical breakdown
senses.definitionCN: 通过减小颗粒尺寸，使微生物得以完成化学分解的动物
senses.example: Detritivores and decomposers together return the forest's nutrients.
senses.exampleCN: 食碎屑动物与分解者共同归还森林的养分。
senses.why: The distinction is functional: animals chew and fragment, microbes mineralize, and the two steps complement each other.
senses.whyCN: 这一区分是功能性的：动物咀嚼破碎，微生物矿化，两个步骤彼此补足。

senses.title: A named taxonomic example
senses.definition: a specific group such as isopods, amphipods or dipteran larvae known for detritus feeding
senses.definitionCN: 等足类、端足类或双翅目幼虫等以食碎屑著称的具体类群
senses.example: Amphipods are common detritivores in cold coastal waters.
senses.exampleCN: 端足类是寒冷沿海水域常见的食碎屑动物。
senses.why: Field guides need a label for whole groups whose members share the habit, so the ecological term doubles as a descriptive tag.
senses.whyCN: 野外手册需要给习性相同的整个类群一个标签，因此这个生态学术语也兼作描述性标签。

senses.title: A user of waste in aquaculture
senses.definition: in aquaculture, an animal used to consume leftover feed and organic waste
senses.definitionCN: 水产养殖中用来消耗残饵与有机废弃物的动物
senses.example: The farm added detritivores to clean the pond bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 养殖场加入食碎屑动物来清理池底。
senses.why: Applied ecology turns the feeding habit into a service, and the word names the worker rather than the wild animal.
senses.whyCN: 应用生态学把这种食性变成服务，这个词指的就是「工人」，而不是野生个体。

senses.title: An eater in the fossil record
senses.titleCN: 化石记录中的食碎屑者
senses.definition: a fossil animal inferred to have fed on detritus from its mouthparts or gut contents
senses.definitionCN: 依据口器或肠道内容物推断以碎屑为食的化石动物
senses.example: The trace fossils suggest detritivores worked the ancient sea floor.
senses.exampleCN: 这些遗迹化石表明食碎屑动物曾在古代海底活动。
senses.why: Paleoecology reconstructs feeding from preserved traces, so the term describes an inferred role rather than an observed one.
senses.whyCN: 古生态学从保存下来的痕迹重建取食行为，因此这个词描述的是推断出的角色，而不是观察到的角色。

intro.en: Detritivore is a twentieth-century scientific compound: detritus plus the -vore ending for eaters.
intro.cn: detritivore 是 20 世纪的科学复合词：detritus 加上表示取食者的 -vore 词尾。

items.en: Detritus is the past participle of Latin deterere, 'to rub away' (de- 'away' + terere 'to rub'). It names material worn off a larger body.
items.cn: detritus 是拉丁语 deterere「磨掉」的过去分词（de-「离开」+ terere「摩擦」），指从更大物体上磨下来的材料。

items.en: The -vore ending comes from Latin vorare, 'to devour', the same root as voracious and carnivore.
items.cn: -vore 词尾来自拉丁语 vorare「吞食」，与 voracious、carnivore 同根。

items.en: The -i- between the two parts is a Latin stem vowel, as in insectivore and frugivore; it is not a separate morpheme.
items.cn: 两部分之间的 -i- 是拉丁词干元音，如 insectivore、frugivore；它并不是独立的语素。

items.en: The term became standard in ecology in the twentieth century, when feeding roles were separated from taxonomic groups. The exact first use is not firmly established.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个词在生态学中成为标准术语，当时取食角色开始与分类群分开讨论。确切首见出处尚无定论。

items.en: Stream and soil ecology adopted detritivore to describe shredders and soil animals, giving the word a practical field meaning.
items.cn: 溪流与土壤生态学采用 detritivore 描述撕碎者与土壤动物，使这个词获得了野外实践意义。

note.en: The first group shares the pieces; the second holds other feeding roles.
note.cn: 第一组共享构词成分；第二组是其他取食角色。

entries.definition: Describes the diet; detritivore is the animal itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述食性；detritivore 指动物本身。

entries.definition: The habit or process of eating detritus, not the eater.
entries.definitionCN: 指食碎屑的习性过程，不是取食者。

entries.definition: The dead fragments themselves; the animal is named after them.
entries.definitionCN: 指死亡碎片本身；动物以它们命名。

entries.definition: A microbe that mineralizes dead matter; a detritivore chews particles but leaves the chemistry to microbes.
entries.definitionCN: 把死亡物质矿化的微生物；食碎屑动物咀嚼颗粒，化学分解则留给微生物。

entries.definition: An animal feeding on dead bodies; detritivores take plant and particle fragments as well as animal remains.
entries.definitionCN: 以尸体为食的动物；食碎屑动物还取食植物与颗粒碎片。

entries.definition: An animal that feeds on living plants or algae; detritivores feed on what is already dead.
entries.definitionCN: 取食活植物或藻类的动物；食碎屑动物取食已经死去的材料。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the food word plus the eater ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：食物名词加取食者词尾。

normal.en: detritus + -vore: a detritus-eater, exactly parallel to insectivore.
normal.cn: detritus + -vore：食碎屑者，与 insectivore 构词完全平行。

normal.en: Typical examples are earthworms, woodlice, caddis larvae and amphipods.
normal.cn: 典型例子有蚯蚓、潮虫、石蛾幼虫与端足类。

normal.en: The phrase detritus food chain names the pathway that starts with dead matter.
normal.cn: detritus food chain 指以死亡物质为起点的食物链路径。

normal.en: The word draws the line against decomposer and scavenger.
normal.cn: 这个词与 decomposer、scavenger 划出了界限。

normal.en: The -i- is a stem vowel, not a separate piece of meaning.
normal.cn: -i- 是词干元音，并不是独立的意义单位。

abstract.en: Think of a kitchen where nobody cooks: the staff only reheat what yesterday left behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一间没人做饭的厨房：员工只把昨天剩下的东西重新加热。

abstract.en: A detritivore is a paper shredder that also eats the paper.
abstract.cn: 食碎屑动物就是一台把纸碎掉、还把纸吃掉的碎纸机。

abstract.en: In a stream, dead leaves are the harvest, and the shredders are the mill.
abstract.cn: 在溪流里，落叶是收成，撕碎者就是磨坊。

examples.en: Detritivores speed up decay by cutting large fragments into small ones.
examples.cn: 食碎屑动物把大碎片切成小碎片，从而加快腐烂。

examples.en: The pond's detritivores keep the bottom from sealing under uneaten feed.
examples.cn: 池塘里的食碎屑动物防止池底被剩余饲料封住。

examples.en: Trace fossils show that detritivores were active in the ancient sediment.
examples.cn: 遗迹化石表明食碎屑动物曾在古代沉积物中活动。

dict_mnemonic.text: detritus（碎屑）+ vore（吞食者）→ 吃碎屑的动物

root: 拉丁语 detritus「被磨掉的东西」（deterere 的过去分词，de- + terere「摩擦」）+ 拉丁语 vorare「吞食」+ -ore → detritivore「吞食碎屑者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one relation: an animal and the dead fragments it eats. The setting may be a stream, soil, a feeding guild, a farm pond or a fossil bed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都保持同一个关系：动物与它取食的死亡碎片。场景可以是溪流、土壤、取食功能群、养殖池塘或化石层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small animal turning dead fragments into its own body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只小动物把死亡碎片转化为自己的身体。

branches.en: THE CORE: the diet defines the animal, and the setting decides whether it shreds, mixes or grazes fragments.
branches.cn: 核心：食性定义了动物，而环境决定它是在撕碎、混合还是刮食碎片。

branches.en: THE GUILD: ecology groups all detritus feeders together regardless of species.
branches.cn: 功能群：生态学把所有食碎屑者归为一组，不论物种。

branches.en: THE DIVISION OF LABOUR: animals fragment, microbes mineralize.
branches.cn: 分工：动物负责破碎，微生物负责矿化。

branches.en: THE NAMED USERS: field guides name typical groups, and aquaculture employs them as cleaners.
branches.cn: 具名使用者：野外手册列出典型类群，水产养殖则把它们雇为清道夫。

branches.en: THE PAST: trace fossils let paleontologists infer the same role in ancient sediments.
branches.cn: 过去：遗迹化石让古生物学家在古代沉积物中推断出同样的角色。

intro.en: Detritivore is a compound of a Latin participle-noun and a Latin eating root.
intro.cn: detritivore 由拉丁语分词名词与拉丁语「吃」的词根复合而成。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are detritus 'rubbed-away material' and vorare 'to devour'; the linking -i- is a stem vowel.
latinIntro.cn: 成分是 detritus「被磨掉的材料」与 vorare「吞食」；连接元音 -i- 是词干元音。

items.example: The detritivore hides under the leaf mat.
items.exampleCN: 这种食碎屑动物藏在叶垫下面。

items.example: The detritivorous shrimp grazes the bottom.
items.exampleCN: 这种食碎屑的虾在底部觅食。

items.example: Detritivory dominates in headwater streams.
items.exampleCN: 食碎屑在溪流源头占主导。

items.example: Detritus collects behind the fallen branch.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑积聚在倒下的树枝后面。

items.example: Detrital food webs begin with dead matter.
items.exampleCN: 碎屑食物网以死亡物质为起点。

items.example: Herbivore and detritivore differ in what is alive.
items.exampleCN: 食草者与食碎屑者的区别在于食物是否还活着。

items.example: Carnivore is the third classic feeding type.
items.exampleCN: 食肉者是第三种经典的食性类型。

items.example: Voracious and detritivore share the eating root.
items.exampleCN: voracious 与 detritivore 共享「吃」的词根。

definition_zh: 反射；反射动作；本能反应；反光式（摄影）；反射的：神经系统对刺激作出的不随意快速反应，也指光线折返的装置
definition_en: an automatic, rapid nervous response to a stimulus, or a device that turns light back, or the adjective describing such a response
core_image: 膝头被小锤轻敲，小腿自行弹起，动作在意识跟上之前就已经完成
scene: 小锤轻敲膝头，小腿自行弹起，等意识到时动作已经完成。 The doctor tapped the tendon to check that the reflex was intact.
sceneCN: 这里指神经系统对敲击作出的不随意快速反应（第 1 个义项：神经反射）；句意为医生敲击肌腱以检查反射是否完好。

derivatives.zh: reflex + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 反身的；反射性的
reflex + -ly（方式副词）→ 以反射的方式
reflex + -ology（学科）→ 以反射解释行为的学说，语义偏移为「反射学」
reflectere 去词尾 → 折回；反光，是 reflex 的同源动词
reflect + -ion（动作或结果）→ 折回；反光，语义偏移为「沉思」

senses.title: An automatic nervous response
senses.definition: a rapid, involuntary response of a nerve or muscle to a stimulus, mediated by a reflex arc
senses.definitionCN: 神经或肌肉对刺激作出的快速、不随意反应，由反射弧介导
senses.example: The knee reflex disappeared after the nerve was damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 神经受损后，膝反射消失了。
senses.why: Latin reflexus is 'bent back', because the impulse is imagined as turning back from the muscle to the cord.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 reflexus 意为「折回」，因为冲动被想象为从肌肉折回脊髓。

senses.title: An unthinking reaction
senses.definition: an immediate response made before reflection, often emotional or habitual
senses.definitionCN: 在思考之前作出的即时回应，常带情绪或习惯性
senses.example: Apology was a reflex, not a considered decision.
senses.exampleCN: 道歉是本能反应，不是经过考虑的决定。
senses.why: the bodily image transferred to conduct: an answer that comes back before thought does.
senses.whyCN: 身体形象转移到举止上：回答在思考之前就回来了。

senses.title: A reflex movement
senses.definition: a movement produced by a reflex rather than by intention, such as blinking or withdrawing a hand
senses.definitionCN: 由反射而非意图产生的动作，如眨眼或缩手
senses.example: The withdrawal reflex moved his hand before he saw the flame.
senses.exampleCN: 他看见火焰之前，缩手反射已经把他的手移开了。
senses.why: the noun names the whole event, so the movement itself can be called a reflex.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名整个事件，因此动作本身也能被称为反射。

senses.title: The reflex arc
senses.definition: the neural pathway from sensory receptor through the spinal cord to the muscle that carries out the response
senses.definitionCN: 从感受器经脊髓到执行反应肌肉的神经通路
senses.example: The reflex arc bypasses the brain and saves precious milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 反射弧绕过大脑，省下宝贵的毫秒。
senses.why: physiology needed a name for the circuit, and the whole event's name was extended to its wiring.
senses.whyCN: 生理学需要给这条回路一个名字，整个事件的名字便被扩展到它的线路。

senses.title: An unconditioned response in psychology
senses.titleCN: 心理学中的无条件反射
senses.definition: a response that occurs naturally to a stimulus without prior learning, as salivation to food
senses.definitionCN: 无需先前学习、对刺激自然发生的反应，如见食物分泌唾液
senses.example: Salivation to food is the classic unconditioned reflex.
senses.exampleCN: 见食物流涎是经典的无条件反射。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the physiological term to name the unlearned half of conditioning.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用生理学术语，命名条件作用中未经学习的那一半。

senses.title: A reflex camera
senses.definition: a camera in which a mirror redirects the image to the viewfinder before the shot
senses.definitionCN: 拍摄前用反光镜把影像送到取景器的相机
senses.example: The reflex camera let her see exactly what the lens saw.
senses.exampleCN: 反光式相机让她准确看到镜头所见的画面。
senses.why: here reflex keeps its optical sense: light is turned back into the photographer's eye.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 reflex 保留光学义：光被折回摄影者眼中。

senses.title: Light bent back
senses.definition: light or an image returned from a surface, the older optical sense of the word
senses.definitionCN: 从表面返回的光或影像，是该词较早的光学义
senses.example: The reflex of the sun on the water blinded the rowers.
senses.exampleCN: 水面反照的阳光使划船者目眩。
senses.why: the optical sense came first in English, and the nervous sense borrowed its name from it.
senses.whyCN: 光学义在英语中先出现，神经义则借用了它的名字。

senses.title: The adjective for automatic responses
senses.definition: describing an action that occurs automatically in answer to a stimulus
senses.definitionCN: 描述对刺激自动发生的动作
senses.example: A reflex blink protected the eye from the dust.
senses.exampleCN: 一次反射性眨眼保护了眼睛免受灰尘侵扰。
senses.why: English lets the noun work as an attributive adjective, so the same form labels the kind of response.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许名词作定语形容词，因此同一形式也能标记反应的种类。

intro.en: Reflex comes from Latin reflexus, the past participle of reflectere 'to bend back'. The optical sense came first in English and the nervous sense followed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: reflex 来自拉丁 reflexus，即 reflectere「折回」的过去分词。英语中先出现光学义，神经义则在 19 世纪跟进。年代为约数。

items.en: Flectere meant 'to bend, curve, turn'. Its compounds describe bending something in a chosen direction.
items.cn: flectere 意为「弯、曲、转」。其复合词描述把某物朝某个方向弯折。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus flectere gave reflectere 'to bend back, turn back', used of light, water and the mind alike.
items.cn: re-「回」加 flectere 构成 reflectere「折回、转回」，光、水面与心智都用这个词。

items.en: The past participle reflexus meant 'bent back', and as a noun it named a bending back, including the turning back of light.
items.cn: 过去分词 reflexus 意为「被折回的」，作名词时指折返，包括光的折回。

items.en: English reflex appeared in the sixteenth century for light or an image turned back from a surface, a sense now mostly carried by reflection.
items.cn: 英语 reflex 在 16 世纪出现，指从表面折回的光或影像，这一义如今主要由 reflection 承担。

items.en: In the nineteenth century physiology gave reflex its nervous sense, and psychology added the conditioned reflex in the early twentieth.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学赋予 reflex 神经义，心理学在 20 世纪初加上条件反射。

items.en: Source uncertain (first physiological use in English): the term spread through nineteenth-century medical writing, and no single first citation is settled; the exact date of the camera sense is also approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语生理义的首见）：这个术语经 19 世纪医学写作扩散，没有公认的首次书证；相机义的确切年代亦为约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same reflect stem that name different things; group two holds other automatic or involuntary responses.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 reflect 词干、命名不同事物的形式；第二组是其他自动或不随意的反应。

entries.definition: The noun for light turned back or for careful thought; it does not name a nervous response.
entries.definitionCN: 指折回的光或深思的名词，不指神经反应。

entries.definition: An adjective for words or relations that turn back on their subject; it is not the noun for a knee jerk.
entries.definitionCN: 指回指主语的词或关系的形容词，不是指膝跳的名词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning 'to bend back' or 'to think carefully'; the noun reflex is a different part of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「折回」或「深思」的动词；名词 reflex 属于不同词类。

entries.definition: An inborn pattern of behaviour common to a species; it is broader and less mechanical than a single reflex.
entries.definitionCN: 物种共有的先天行为模式，比单次反射更宽泛，也不那么机械。

entries.definition: Any response to an event, including deliberate ones; a reflex is specifically automatic and fast.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的任何回应，包括有意的；reflex 特指自动且快速的那一种。

entries.definition: A response acquired through pairing; it is the learned counterpart of the unlearned reflex.
entries.definitionCN: 通过配对习得的反应，是先天反射的学习对应物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real medical collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实医学搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus flectere 'bend': a reflex is a bend back along the same wire.
normal.cn: re-「回」加 flectere「弯」：反射就是沿同一根线折回去。

normal.en: The family runs reflect, reflection, reflexive, reflexly, reflexology.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reflect、reflection、reflexive、reflexly、reflexology。

normal.en: Fixed medical phrases: knee-jerk reflex, reflex action, test a reflex.
normal.cn: 固定医学搭配：膝跳反射、反射动作、检查反射。

normal.en: The optical sense survives in reflex camera, where a mirror turns light back.
normal.cn: 光学义存留在 reflex camera 里，那里的反光镜把光折回。

normal.en: The contrast is conditioned reflex, which is learned rather than wired in.
normal.cn: 对照项是条件反射，它是学来的，而非天生接好的。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer tapping a knee and the leg answering on its own.
abstract.cn: 想象小锤敲一下膝盖，腿自己作出回答。

abstract.en: Picture a wire that loops from muscle back to cord without passing the brain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从肌肉绕回脊髓，不经过大脑。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror in a camera turning the world back into your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象相机里的一面镜子把世界折回你的眼睛。

examples.en: The reflex was tested on both sides for comparison.
examples.cn: 为作比较，两侧都检查了反射。

examples.en: Years of practice had made the movement a reflex.
examples.cn: 多年练习已使这个动作成为本能反应。

examples.en: The reflex camera became standard for press photographers.
examples.cn: 反光式相机成为新闻摄影的标准设备。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（回）+ flex（弯）＝ 折回去；记「锤敲膝盖，腿自己弹起」。

root: 拉丁 re-「回」+ flectere「弯、转」→ reflectere「折回」，过去分词 reflexus「被折回的」；英语先用于光学，19 世纪转用于神经反应。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bend: an impulse turns back, the movement happens, the circuit is mapped, the learned version appears, and the same optical bend survives in cameras and sunlight.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一次折返展开：冲动折回、动作发生、回路被画出、学习版本出现，而同一种光学折返仍活在相机与阳光里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hammer taps a tendon, and the leg answers before the person notices.
core.cn: 核心意象：小锤敲在肌腱上，腿在人察觉之前就作出回答。

branches.en: THE NERVE: the core is a quick involuntary answer carried by a nerve.
branches.cn: 神经：核心是由神经传导的快速不随意回答。

branches.en: HABIT AND BODY: an unthinking answer in speech and a withdrawal of the hand are the same speed seen twice.
branches.cn: 习惯与身体：言语中的不假思索与手的缩回，是同一种速度的两种表现。

branches.en: WIRING AND LEARNING: the arc explains the circuit, and the unconditioned response marks what needs no training.
branches.cn: 线路与学习：反射弧解释回路，无条件反射标记无需训练的部分。

branches.en: LIGHT: a mirror in a camera and the sun on water both bend light back to the eye.
branches.cn: 光：相机里的镜子与水面上的阳光，都把光折回眼睛。

branches.en: THE ADJECTIVE: the same form labels any response that comes automatically.
branches.cn: 形容词：同一形式标记任何自动发生的反应。

intro.en: Reflex is a Latin participle used as an English noun and adjective, and its root builds a family through the verb reflect.
intro.cn: reflex 是拉丁分词，在英语中作名词与形容词，其词根通过动词 reflect 建起一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flectere 'to bend' and re- 'back' build reflectere, reflexus and reflexio; the same root appears in flexible and inflection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flectere「弯」与 re-「回」构成 reflectere、reflexus 与 reflexio；同一词根还出现在 flexible 与 inflection 中。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of bending.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把弯折的方向反过来。

items.structure: flectere, flexi, flexum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root also gives flexible and inflection.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 flexible 与 inflection。

items.example: The verb covers light, water and thought.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词覆盖光、水面与思想。

items.example: The participle is the direct source of reflex.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词是 reflex 的直接来源。

items.meaning: an automatic response or a turned-back light
items.example: English added the nervous sense in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 英语在 19 世纪加上神经义。

items.example: The suffix carries the grammar and logic senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀承载语法与逻辑义。

items.example: The adverb is rare but regular.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词罕见但合乎规则。

items.meaning: a theory explaining behaviour by reflexes
items.meaningCN: 以反射解释行为的学说
items.example: The word later also named foot massage, an unrelated use.
items.exampleCN: 这个词后来也指足部按摩，属无关用法。

items.meaning: a turning back of light; careful thought
items.example: The noun now carries most of the optical sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词如今承担大部分光学义。

definition_zh: 磷循环（磷在岩石、土壤、水体与生物体之间迁移周转的过程，以沉积循环为主要特征）
definition_en: the movement of phosphorus among rocks, soils, water and living organisms, driven mainly by weathering and sedimentation
core_image: 山岩被雨水慢慢啃蚀，磷随泥沙进入土壤与河流，被植物吸走、被动物吃掉，随遗体沉入海底压成新岩，直到地壳抬升再露出地面
scene: 老师在图上画出一条从山岩到海底、再被抬回地面的长线。 Weathering of apatite rock is the only natural entry into the phosphorus cycle.
sceneCN: 这里 phosphorus cycle 指「磷在岩石、水体与生物之间迁移的整个循环」（第 1 个义项：作为整体过程）；句意为磷灰石岩石的风化是磷循环唯一的天然入口。

pos.zh: 磷循环（术语短语，常带定冠词；复数直接加 -s 指不同系统或地质时期的循环）

collocations.phrase: human impact on the phosphorus cycle

derivatives.zh: 希腊 phōsphoros（「带光者」，晨星之名）→ 磷：发光而得名
phosphorus + -ate（化学盐类后缀）→ 磷酸盐：磷在土壤与水中的主要存在形式
phosphate + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 含磷酸盐的
phosphorus + -escent（「正在呈现」）→ 发冷光的：不是燃烧而是缓慢发光的
weather（古英语「天气、风化」）+ -ing → 风化：岩石在原地被水与空气分解
sediment（拉丁 sedimentum「沉降物」）+ -ation → 沉积：颗粒沉落并层层堆积
eu-（希腊「良好」）+ trophē（「营养」）+ -ation → 富营养化：养分过多导致藻类暴发

senses.title: The loop as a whole
senses.definition: the full circuit that moves phosphorus from rock through life and water and back into rock
senses.definitionCN: 让磷从岩石穿过生命与水体、再回到岩石的完整回路
senses.example: Weathering of apatite rock is the only natural entry into the phosphorus cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 磷灰石岩石的风化是磷循环唯一的天然入口。
senses.why: the phrase names the whole circuit, which here is mostly a sedimentary one.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语命名的是整个回路，而这里它主要是一条沉积回路。

senses.title: Weathering as the source
senses.definition: the slow release of phosphate from apatite and other minerals as rock breaks down
senses.definitionCN: 岩石分解时磷灰石等矿物缓慢释放磷酸盐
senses.example: Without weathering the phosphorus cycle would have no new supply.
senses.exampleCN: 没有风化，磷循环就没有新的补给。
senses.why: phosphorus has no gaseous phase, so the loop must start with solid rock being broken.
senses.whyCN: 磷没有气态阶段，所以循环必须从固体岩石被分解开始。

senses.title: Plant uptake
senses.definition: the uptake of dissolved phosphate by roots, often assisted by mycorrhizal fungi
senses.definitionCN: 根系吸收溶解态磷酸盐，常由菌根真菌协助
senses.example: Mycorrhizal fungi extend the reach of plant uptake in the phosphorus cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 菌根真菌在磷循环中扩大了植物吸收的范围。
senses.why: phosphate is scarce and immobile in soil, so plants must partner with fungi to reach it.
senses.whyCN: 磷酸盐在土壤中稀少且不易移动，植物必须与真菌合作才能取得。

senses.title: Transfer through the food chain
senses.definition: the passage of phosphorus from plants to herbivores and predators, concentrated at each step
senses.definitionCN: 磷从植物到食草动物再到捕食者的传递，每一步都富集
senses.example: Each trophic step in the phosphorus cycle passes on a smaller total but a richer concentration.
senses.exampleCN: 磷循环中每个营养级传下去的总量更少，浓度却更高。
senses.why: phosphorus builds bones, teeth and DNA, so bodies keep and concentrate it as it moves up.
senses.whyCN: 磷构成骨骼、牙齿与遗传物质，所以它在向上传递时被身体保留并富集。

senses.title: Decomposition and return
senses.definition: the release of phosphate when dead tissue and waste are broken down
senses.definitionCN: 死亡组织与排泄物被分解时释放磷酸盐
senses.example: Decomposition closes the short loop of the phosphorus cycle within a forest floor.
senses.exampleCN: 分解在林地上层闭合了磷循环的短回路。
senses.why: most phosphate is recycled quickly, so the loop has a tight biological circle inside the slow rock one.
senses.whyCN: 大部分磷酸盐被迅速回收，于是循环在缓慢的岩石回路里还套着一个紧密的生物圈。

senses.title: Sedimentation and burial
senses.definition: the sinking of phosphate particles to the seabed and their consolidation into new rock
senses.definitionCN: 含磷颗粒沉到海底并固结成新岩石
senses.example: Sedimentation removes phosphate from the ocean over geological time.
senses.exampleCN: 在地质时间尺度上，沉积把磷酸盐从海洋中移走。
senses.why: the loop's exit is the sea floor, where the element is locked into sediment.
senses.whyCN: 循环的出口是海底，元素在那里被锁进沉积物。

senses.title: Uplift and the long return
senses.definition: the tectonic rise of phosphate-bearing rock that makes the element available again
senses.definitionCN: 含磷岩石经构造抬升重新变得可用
senses.example: Tectonic uplift restarts the phosphorus cycle after millions of years.
senses.exampleCN: 构造抬升在数百万年后重新启动磷循环。
senses.why: burial would end the story, so the loop depends on mountains rising out of old seabeds.
senses.whyCN: 埋藏本该结束一切，因此循环依赖旧海底升成山脉。

senses.title: Scarcity and fertiliser
senses.definition: the mining of phosphate rock and guano to supplement a naturally tight supply
senses.definitionCN: 开采磷矿石与鸟粪石以补充天然的紧供给
senses.example: Modern agriculture runs the phosphorus cycle at twice its natural pace.
senses.exampleCN: 现代农业让磷循环以天然速度的两倍运转。
senses.why: because the natural flow is so small, farming had to open a new industrial inflow.
senses.whyCN: 正因为天然流量如此之小，农业不得不开一个工业的新流入。

senses.title: Runoff and eutrophication
senses.definition: the leakage of excess phosphate into rivers and lakes, where it feeds algal blooms
senses.definitionCN: 过量磷酸盐漏入河流湖泊，喂养藻类暴发
senses.example: Farm runoff adds a shortcut to the phosphorus cycle that ends in dead lakes.
senses.exampleCN: 农田径流给磷循环加了一条以死湖收尾的捷径。
senses.why: the element that limits growth in most fresh waters becomes a pollutant once it arrives in surplus.
senses.whyCN: 在多数淡水中限制生长的元素，一旦过量到达便成了污染物。

intro.en: Phosphorus cycle joins a Greek name for the morning star to a Greek word for a wheel. Phosphorus means 'light-bearer', from phōs 'light' and pherein 'to carry'. The element was isolated about 1669 because it glowed in the dark; cycle came through Latin cyclus from Greek kyklos.
intro.cn: phosphorus cycle 把希腊语的晨星之名接在希腊语的轮子上。phosphorus 意为「带光者」，来自 phōs「光」与 pherein「携带」。这种元素约在一六六九年因在暗处发光而被分离出来；cycle 经拉丁 cyclus 来自希腊 kyklos。

items.en: Phōsphoros, 'light-bearer', named the planet Venus as the morning star; Latin took it as Phosphorus.
items.cn: phōsphoros「带光者」是金星作为晨星的名字；拉丁语借作 Phosphorus。

items.en: A glowing substance isolated from urine around 1669 was given the name of the light-bearer, and the element kept it.
items.cn: 约一六六九年从尿液中分离出的发光物质被冠以「带光者」之名，这种元素沿用至今。

items.en: Kyklos 'circle, wheel' passed through Latin cyclus into English cycle.
items.cn: kyklos「圆圈、轮子」经拉丁 cyclus 进入英语 cycle。

items.en: Liebig's mineral theory established phosphorus as a limiting plant nutrient, making its circulation a subject of agricultural chemistry.
items.cn: 李比希的矿物营养理论确立磷为限制性植物养分，使磷的流转成为农业化学的课题。

items.en: Twentieth-century soil science and limnology named the sedimentary circuit of phosphorus a cycle, in deliberate contrast to the gaseous nitrogen cycle.
items.cn: 二十世纪的土壤学与湖沼学把磷的沉积回路称为循环，以与气态的氮循环形成对照。

items.en: Research on lake pollution tied the phrase to phosphate runoff and algal blooms.
items.cn: 湖泊污染研究把这个短语与磷酸盐径流和藻类暴发联系起来。

note.en: Group one holds the phosphorus compounds and processes most easily confused with the cycle; group two holds the cycling terms it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易与磷循环混淆的磷类化合物与过程；第二组是常与它比较的循环术语。

entries.definition: A salt or ester of phosphoric acid; it is the form phosphorus takes in soil and water, not the circulation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 磷酸的盐或酯；它是磷在土壤与水中的存在形式，而非流转过程本身。

entries.definition: Glowing without heat; the adjective recalls the element's discovery but says nothing about nutrient movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不发热的发光；这个形容词让人想起该元素的发现，与养分迁移无关。

entries.definition: Nutrient over-enrichment that causes algal blooms; excess phosphate triggers it but it is not the cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 养分过度富集引发藻类暴发；过量磷酸盐会触发它，但它不是循环。

entries.definition: A phosphate mineral that holds most rock phosphorus; it is the starting store, not the loop.
entries.definitionCN: 一种磷酸盐矿物，容纳大部分岩石磷；它是起始储库，不是循环。

entries.definition: The general circulation of a nutrient through organisms and environment; phosphorus is one case.
entries.definitionCN: 养分在生物与环境中的一般循环；磷循环是其中一个例子。

entries.definition: A cycle whose main store is rock rather than air; the phosphorus cycle is the textbook example.
entries.definitionCN: 主要储库是岩石而非空气的循环；磷循环是教科书例子。

entries.definition: The general class of element cycles driven by life, rock and chemistry; it includes phosphorus.
entries.definitionCN: 由生命、岩石与化学驱动的元素循环大类；包含磷循环。

entries.definition: The circulation of nitrogen, whose huge atmospheric store makes it far faster than the rock-bound phosphorus cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 氮的循环，其巨大的大气储库使它远比受岩石束缚的磷循环快。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek roots and the real sedimentary route.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根与真实的沉积路径。

normal.en: Phosphorus is phōsphoros, 'light-bearer': the element glows, and the morning star carries the same name.
normal.cn: phosphorus 即 phōsphoros「带光者」：元素会发光，晨星也用同一个名字。

normal.en: No gas phase: phosphorus travels by rock, not by air, so its cycle is slow.
normal.cn: 没有气态：磷靠岩石而非空气旅行，所以它的循环很慢。

normal.en: Start at the quarry: weathering releases phosphate, everything else follows.
normal.cn: 从采石场想起：风化释放磷酸盐，其余环节随之而来。

normal.en: Four stops: rock, root, animal, seabed, then uplift back to rock.
normal.cn: 四站：岩石、根、动物、海底，然后抬升回到岩石。

normal.en: Guano and phosphate rock are the two mined shortcuts into the loop.
normal.cn: 鸟粪石与磷矿石是进入这个循环的两条采矿捷径。

abstract.en: The phosphorus cycle is a mountain slowly walking to the sea and back.
abstract.cn: 磷循环是一座慢慢走向大海又走回来的山。

abstract.en: It is a budget with no income except erosion.
abstract.cn: 它是一份除了侵蚀别无收入的预算。

abstract.en: Life borrows the same few atoms of phosphorus over and over.
abstract.cn: 生命一遍又一遍地借用同一些磷原子。

examples.en: Phosphate fertiliser has roughly doubled the natural flow of the phosphorus cycle.
examples.cn: 磷肥使磷循环的天然流量大约翻了一倍。

examples.en: Because the phosphorus cycle lacks a gas phase, it responds slowly to change.
examples.cn: 由于磷循环没有气态阶段，它对变化的回应很慢。

examples.en: Scientists study the phosphorus cycle to predict when reserves of phosphate rock will run short.
examples.cn: 科学家研究磷循环，以预测磷矿石储量何时会短缺。

dict_mnemonic.text: phosphorus（磷，意为带光者）+ cycle（循环）＝磷从岩石出发、经植物与动物、沉到海底再抬升回来；记它没有气态，所以特别慢。

root: phosphorus（希腊 phōsphoros「带光者」，phōs「光」+ pherein「携带」）+ cycle（希腊 kyklos「圆环」经拉丁 cyclus）；短语为二十世纪土壤学与湖沼学所立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow the slow sedimentary route: the whole loop, weathering, uptake, food chain, decay, burial, uplift, scarcity and runoff.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿缓慢的沉积路径展开：整体、风化、吸收、食物链、腐烂、埋藏、抬升、稀缺，以及径流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: rain cracks apatite, roots take the phosphate, animals pass it on, dead matter sinks to the seabed, and uplift brings the rock back to the surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨水劈开磷灰石，根吸走磷酸盐，动物把它传下去，遗体沉到海底，抬升再把岩石带回地表。

branches.en: WHOLE AND DEEP TIME: the circuit as one object, then the tectonic return that completes it.
branches.cn: 整体与深时：先是作为一个对象的回路，再是完成它的构造回归。

branches.en: FROM ROCK TO ROOT: weathering opens the supply, fungi help roots take it.
branches.cn: 从岩石到根：风化打开供给，真菌帮根系取得。

branches.en: THROUGH BODIES: transfer up the food chain, then release by decay.
branches.cn: 穿过身体：沿食物链上移，再经腐烂释放。

branches.en: BURIAL: phosphate sinking and hardening into future rock.
branches.cn: 埋藏：磷酸盐下沉并固结成未来的岩石。

branches.en: HUMAN USE AND LEAK: mined supplements, then runoff that feeds algal blooms.
branches.cn: 人类取用与泄漏：先是采矿补充，再是喂养藻华的径流。

intro.en: Phosphorus cycle is a two-word technical phrase: a Greek name for the morning star plus a Greek noun for recurrence.
intro.cn: phosphorus cycle 是两词技术短语：希腊语的晨星之名，加一个希腊语源名词表示周而复始。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed Greek Phosphorus as a proper name and Greek kyklos as cyclus, so both halves reached English through Latin channels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊 Phosphorus 作专名，也借入 kyklos 作 cyclus，所以两半都经拉丁渠道到达英语。
