sceneCN: 这里指把分散的部门与账目合成一个整体（第 2 个义项：把多个单位并入一个机构）；句意：这两家公司把仓库与账目合并成一套系统。

senses.title: To make ground or a structure firm
senses.definition: to press loose material or a built structure until it can carry weight without shifting
senses.definitionCN: 把松散的材料或已建的结构压紧，使其承重而不位移
senses.example: Workers consolidate the soil before the foundation is laid.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在打地基之前先把土层压实。
senses.why: The Latin adjective inside the verb means solid, so the first sense is simply to make something solid.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词里的拉丁形容词意为坚实，因此第一个义项就是使某物变坚实。

senses.title: To merge separate units into one
senses.definition: to combine two or more organizations, departments or functions into a single body
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多组织、部门或职能合成一个机构
senses.example: The two firms consolidate their warehouses and accounts into one system.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家公司把仓库与账目合并成一套系统。
senses.why: Units made solid by being joined cannot be pulled apart again, so merging is pictured as hardening.
senses.whyCN: 各单位一旦合成一体便再难拆开，因此合并被想象成变硬的过程。

senses.title: To secure power or control
senses.definition: to make a hold on power or authority firmer and less easy to shake
senses.definitionCN: 使对权力或权威的掌握更牢固、更难动摇
senses.example: The new mayor spent the first year consolidating her support.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长用第一年巩固自己的支持基础。
senses.why: Power that is solid cannot be shaken, so securing it is described as making it solid.
senses.whyCN: 权力若坚实便难以撼动，因此稳固权力就被说成使之坚实。

senses.title: To combine debts or financial claims
senses.definition: to roll several loans or claims into one obligation with a single schedule
senses.definitionCN: 把多笔贷款或债权并成一项义务，只用一张还款表
senses.example: The family consolidated three credit cards into one loan.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把三张信用卡的欠款并成一笔贷款。
senses.why: Several debts are pressed into one solid block, which is easier to carry and to count.
senses.whyCN: 多笔债务被压成一块整块，既好背负，也好计算。

senses.title: To make learning durable
senses.definition: to repeat and reorganize knowledge until it resists forgetting
senses.definitionCN: 反复复习并重新组织知识，使其不易被遗忘
senses.example: Short daily reviews consolidate what the students learned in class.
senses.exampleCN: 每天短时复习能巩固学生在课堂上学到的东西。
senses.why: A memory becomes solid when repeated practice closes the gaps between its pieces.
senses.whyCN: 反复练习填上记忆碎片之间的缝隙，记忆才变得坚实。

senses.title: To merge scattered records
senses.titleCN: 把分散的记录整合起来
senses.definition: to gather records kept in different places into one store that can be searched as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把存放在不同地点的记录汇入一个可整体检索的库
senses.example: The hospital consolidated patient files from five clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院把五个诊所的病人档案整合到一起。
senses.why: Scattered records are like loose bricks; putting them in one store is pressing them into a block.
senses.whyCN: 分散的记录如同散砖，汇入一处就是把它们压成一整块。

senses.title: To lock in a gain or result
senses.definition: to protect a success already won so that it cannot be lost by later change
senses.definitionCN: 保护已经取得的成功，使其不因后续变化而丧失
senses.example: The team consolidated its lead with a second goal.
senses.exampleCN: 球队用第二个进球锁定了领先优势。
senses.why: A win is not safe until it is made firm, so securing a result is called consolidating it.
senses.whyCN: 胜利在变牢之前并不安全，因此保住结果被称为巩固它。

senses.title: Of sediment hardening into rock
senses.definition: in geology, of loose sediment, to harden into rock under pressure and mineral cement
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学中，指松散沉积物在压力与矿物胶结作用下硬结成岩
senses.example: Over millions of years the sand consolidated into sandstone.
senses.exampleCN: 历经数百万年，砂粒固结成了砂岩。
senses.why: Geology kept the most literal sense: loose grains really do become one solid mass.
senses.whyCN: 地质学保留了最字面的含义：松散的颗粒真的会变成一块固体。

intro.en: Consolidate is a Latin verb of solidity: a prefix meaning together and an adjective meaning solid. English took it in the sixteenth century and later stretched it from ground to companies and to memory.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示坚实的拉丁动词：前缀意为一起，形容词意为坚实。英语在十六世纪借入，后来从土地扩展到公司，再扩展到记忆。

items.en: Solidus meant solid, whole and undivided; the adjective is the part that matters for this verb.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词表示坚实的、完整的、不可分的；对这个动词而言，起作用的是形容词义。

items.en: The prefix com- added togetherness and intensity, so the compound meant to make thoroughly solid.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起并加强语气，因此复合词意为彻底使坚实。

items.en: Latin consolidare meant to make firm, and also to knit broken parts into a whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词表示使牢固，也指把破碎的部分接合成整体。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, first for making structures, positions and claims firm.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，先用于使建筑、阵地与主张牢固。

items.en: Banks and companies later used it for pressing many debts or units into one body.
items.cn: 银行与公司后来用它指把多笔债务或多个单位压成一个整体。

items.en: Modern psychology and computing extended it to knowledge and records that must not fall apart.
items.cn: 现代心理学与计算机把它扩展到不可散失的知识与记录。

note.en: The first group shares the solid root or looks close to it; the second group names nearby acts of joining and strengthening.
note.cn: 第一组共享坚实的词根或字形相近；第二组是相邻的连接与加强行为。

entries.definition: The act or result of making firm or of merging units.
entries.definitionCN: 使牢固或合并单位的动作或结果。

entries.definition: Already made firm or already merged, as in consolidated accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 已经变牢或已经合并的，如合并后的账目。

entries.definition: Firm and without gaps; it describes the state the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 坚实而无空隙；描述动词造成的结果状态。

entries.definition: To comfort someone in grief; it comes from a different Latin verb and has nothing to do with solidity.
entries.definitionCN: 在悲伤中安慰某人；出自另一个拉丁动词，与坚实无关。

entries.definition: To join two bodies into one; it names the joining without the idea of hardening.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个主体并为一个；只说合并，不含变硬之意。

entries.definition: To make a thing stronger; it may add force without adding solidity.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物更强；可能增添力量而不增添坚实度。

entries.definition: To make parts share one identity; it stresses unity rather than material firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 使各部分共有一个身份；强调统一，而非材质坚实。

entries.definition: To add support to something already there; extra material is brought in.
entries.definitionCN: 在已有之物上加支撑；强调的是外加材料。

entries.definition: To make a hold safe from loss; it names protection rather than compression.
entries.definitionCN: 使所得免于失去；强调保护，而不是压紧。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the solid root, the real family and the fixed phrases of finance and management.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用坚实的词根、真实同族词，以及金融与管理中的固定搭配。

normal.en: Solidus means solid, so the verb begins as a picture of pressing something firm.
normal.cn: 词根意为坚实，动词最初就是把某物压实的画面。

normal.en: The family runs consolidation, consolidated, consolidator and consolidative.
normal.cn: 同族词有表示合并的名词、已合并的形容词、合并者与起巩固作用的形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: consolidate power, consolidate gains, consolidate debts.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：巩固权力、锁定成果、合并债务。

normal.en: The business sense is the newest common one: units into one body.
normal.cn: 商业义是较晚普及的用法：把单位并成一个主体。

normal.en: The geological sense is the oldest literal one: loose sand into stone.
normal.cn: 地质义是最字面的用法：松散砂粒变成岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a fist closing on a handful of sand until it holds the shape of the fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握紧一把沙，沙被捏成拳头的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a torn map glued back into one sheet with the seams gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张撕裂的地图被粘回一整张，接缝消失。

abstract.en: Picture a dozen voices learning to speak one sentence at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象十几个声音学会在同一时刻说出同一句话。

examples.en: The company consolidated its three regional offices into one headquarters.
examples.cn: 公司把三个地区办事处合并成一个总部。

examples.en: Reviewing the same material twice a week consolidates it in memory.
examples.cn: 每周复习同一材料两次能让它牢牢留在记忆里。

examples.en: The army consolidated its position before the winter set in.
examples.cn: 军队在入冬前巩固了阵地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「梭里得」——把散沙压成一块整石：巩固、合并

root: 拉丁语「一起、加强」前缀加「坚实」一词，构成「使坚实」，十六世纪进入英语；核心是把松散的压成一块整石。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all press loose things into one firm body: ground, companies, power, debts, memory, records, results and stone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把松散之物压成一个坚实整体：土地、公司、权力、债务、记忆、记录、成果与岩石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose bricks pressed into one block, the gaps filled with mortar, impossible to pull apart again.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的砖块被压进一块整石，缝隙里灌满灰浆，再也掰不开。

branches.en: THE LITERAL: loose ground or a built structure made able to carry weight.
branches.cn: 字面义：松散的土层或建筑被压得能够承重。

branches.en: UNITS JOINED: organizations, warehouses and accounts pressed into one body.
branches.cn: 单位合一：组织、仓库与账目被压成一个主体。

branches.en: POWER AND GAINS: control made unshakable and a lead locked in.
branches.cn: 权力与成果：控制变得不可撼动，领先优势被锁定。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: debts rolled into one loan and scattered records into one store.
branches.cn: 账簿：债务并成一笔贷款，分散记录汇入一处。

branches.en: THE MIND AND THE ROCK: durable memory, and sediment hardened into stone.
branches.cn: 心智与岩石：牢固的记忆，以及固结成岩的沉积物。

intro.en: Consolidate is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin adjective and a verb ending, and its family covers finance, management and geology.
intro.cn: 本词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁形容词与动词词尾构成，其词族横跨金融、管理与地质。

latinIntro.en: Latin solidus and the prefix com- are the two pieces inside consolidare; English added the verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示坚实的形容词与表示一起的前缀，是那个拉丁动词内部的两个构件；英语补上了动词词尾。

items.example: It both joins and intensifies the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它既表示结合，也加强那个形容词。

items.example: The adjective supplies the core state.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供核心状态。

items.meaning: to make firm; to knit together
items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接祖形。

items.example: It turns the Latin stem into an English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干变成英语动词。

items.example: It names the merging or the firming.
items.exampleCN: 它指合并或变牢这件事。

items.example: It is the same prefix in another shape.
items.exampleCN: 这是同一前缀的另一种写法。

items.example: It marks the finished state of a merged body.
items.exampleCN: 它标记合并完成后的状态。

items.example: It names the party that carries out a merger.
The finance sense needs this object to appear.
items.exampleCN: 金融义需要这类宾语才能成立。

definition_zh: 海岸带；沿海地带；潮间带及近岸水域；海岸开发区；海岸管理区
definition_en: the belt of land and shallow sea where the coast meets the water, often defined for management
core_image: 一条从崖顶草坡延伸到浅海的窄带，滩面、盐沼与浅水并排铺开
scene: 规划员在潮间带的木桩上系了标记绳，把从最高潮线到浅海的带状区域量进图纸。 The new rules protect the coastal zone from unchecked construction.
sceneCN: 这里指「陆地与海洋交界的带状区域」（第 1 个义项：从受潮汐与海浪影响的陆地一直延伸到近岸浅海的空间带）；句意是新规保护海岸带免受无序建设侵蚀。场景物件：木桩、标记绳、潮线、图纸。

pos.zh: 海岸带；沿海地带（可数；复数 coastal zones）

collocations.phrase: the coastal zone of a delta

senses.title: The land-sea strip
senses.definition: the belt of land and shallow sea where the coast meets the water
senses.definitionCN: 陆地与浅海相接、海岸临水的那条地带
senses.example: The new rules protect the coastal zone from unchecked construction.
senses.exampleCN: 新规保护海岸带免受无序建设侵蚀。
senses.why: Zone names a belt with recognized limits, and coastal fixes one end at the water, so the phrase is the edge treated as an area rather than a line.
senses.whyCN: zone 指有可辨边界的地带，coastal 把一端固定在水中，因此这个短语把边缘当作一片区域而不是一条线。

senses.title: The tidal reach
senses.definition: the part of the coast reached by tides, from the high-water mark to the shallow nearshore
senses.definitionCN: 从高潮线到近岸浅水、受潮汐作用的海岸部分
senses.example: Salt marshes and mudflats share the same coastal zone.
senses.exampleCN: 盐沼与泥滩处在同一条海岸带上。
senses.why: Tides draw a natural boundary twice a day, so the phrase often narrows to the reach that water actually covers.
senses.whyCN: 潮汐每天两次画出天然边界，因此这个短语常收窄到海水实际覆盖的那一段。

senses.title: An ecological ecotone
senses.definition: the transition belt where marine, freshwater and terrestrial habitats overlap
senses.definitionCN: 海洋、淡水与陆地生境相互重叠的过渡地带
senses.example: Migratory birds depend on the coastal zone as a staging ground.
senses.exampleCN: 候鸟依赖海岸带作为中途停歇地。
senses.why: Ecologists saw that the strip is neither sea nor land but a meeting place, so the phrase became a name for an ecotone.
senses.whyCN: 生态学家看出这条带既非海也非陆，而是交汇处，于是这个短语成了生态过渡带的名称。

senses.title: A legal management zone
senses.definition: an area defined by statute for permits, setbacks and coastal planning
senses.definitionCN: 为许可、退让线与海岸规划而由法规划定的区域
senses.example: The coastal zone boundary lies fifty metres inland of the dune crest.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸带边界位于沙丘脊线向内五十米处。
senses.why: Governments needed a mapped limit, so the ecological strip was given a legal boundary and became an administrative zone.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要一条图上界线，于是生态地带被赋予法定边界，成为行政分区。

senses.title: A development corridor
senses.definition: the settled and built-up strip used for ports, tourism and industry
senses.definitionCN: 用于港口、旅游与产业的聚居与建设地带
senses.example: Hotels and marinas now line much of the coastal zone.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆与游艇码头如今排满了海岸带的大部分。
senses.why: Because people want to be near the water, the same belt became an economic corridor, and the phrase followed the money.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们愿意靠近水，同一条带就成了经济走廊，短语也随之跟着资金走。

senses.title: The settled coastal belt
senses.definition: the densely populated strip in which most coastal towns and roads sit
senses.definitionCN: 沿海城镇与道路密集分布的居住地带
senses.example: Most of the country's population lives in the coastal zone.
senses.exampleCN: 该国大部分人口住在海岸带。
senses.why: Statistics treat the strip as a demographic unit, so the phrase can mean the belt where people actually live.
senses.whyCN: 统计把这条带当作人口单元，因此这个短语也可指人们实际居住的地带。

senses.title: A geomorphic unit
senses.definition: a landform system of beach, dune, cliff, marsh and nearshore shelf
senses.definitionCN: 由海滩、沙丘、崖壁、盐沼与近岸陆架构成的地貌系统
senses.example: Each coastal zone has its own balance of erosion and deposition.
senses.exampleCN: 每个海岸带都有自己的侵蚀与沉积平衡。
senses.why: Geomorphologists group the features that share sediment, so the phrase names a process-linked landform unit.
senses.whyCN: 地貌学家把共享沉积物的要素归在一起，因此这个短语指一个与过程相连的地貌单元。

senses.title: Figurative interface
senses.definition: any boundary area where two systems meet and exchange
senses.definitionCN: 任何两个系统相遇并交换物质的边界区域
senses.example: The workshop became a coastal zone between research and policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这场研讨会成了研究与政策之间的「海岸带」。
senses.why: Once the strip is understood as an interface, it can describe any place where two worlds trade, not only land and sea.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这条带被理解为接口，它就能描述任何两个世界互相交换的地方，而不只陆与海。

intro.en: Coastal zone joins Latin costa 'rib, side' to Latin zona 'belt' from Greek zōnē. The compound is a twentieth-century planning term. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: coastal zone 把拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧边」与拉丁 zona「带」并置，后者出自希腊 zōnē。这个复合词是二十世纪的规划术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek zōnē meant a belt or girdle, and geographers used it for the climatic belts of the globe.
items.cn: 希腊 zōnē 指腰带或束带，地理学家用它指地球上的气候带。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as zona and kept both the belt sense and the geographic sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词作 zona，同时保留腰带义与地理带义。

items.en: Costa 'rib, side' gave Old French coste and English coast; the adjective coastal followed with the Latin suffix -alis.
items.cn: costa「肋骨、侧边」形成古法语 coste 与英语 coast；形容词 coastal 随后加上拉丁后缀 -alis。

items.en: English zone first meant a belt on a map, then any area marked off for a purpose, such as a military or customs zone.
items.cn: 英语 zone 最初指地图上的一条带，随后指为某种目的划出的任何区域，如军事区或关税区。

items.en: Coastal zone became common after mid-century coastal management laws, which required states to define the strip they would regulate.
items.cn: 二十世纪中叶海岸管理立法要求各州划定自己要监管的地带之后，coastal zone 开始通行。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of costa is unknown, the pre-Greek source of zōnē is uncertain, and the first printed use of the English phrase is not precisely dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：costa 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，zōnē 的前希腊语来源不确定，英语短语最早的印刷记录也没有确切年代。

note.en: Group one holds same-root belt and coast words that are easily swapped; group two holds other shore strips defined by different processes.
note.cn: 第一组是同根、容易被替换的「带」与「岸」相关词；第二组是按不同过程划分的其他岸边地带。

entries.definition: The land beside the sea, often thought of as a line; a coastal zone is the broader belt on both sides of that line.
entries.definitionCN: 海旁的陆地，常被想成一条线；coastal zone 是这条线两侧更宽的地带。

entries.definition: Relating to the coast; it needs a noun such as zone or town and cannot stand for the area by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与海岸有关的形容词；它需要 zone、town 等名词，不能独自指那片区域。

entries.definition: Any area marked off for a purpose; coastal zone limits the purpose to the shore.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种目的划出的任何区域；coastal zone 把目的限定到海岸。

entries.definition: The legal practice of dividing land into use districts; it acts on the coastal zone but is not the zone itself.
entries.definitionCN: 把土地划为用途分区的法律实践；它作用于海岸带，却不是海岸带本身。

entries.definition: The line where water meets land; it is the inner edge of the coastal zone, not the whole belt.
entries.definitionCN: 水与陆相接的线；它是海岸带的内缘，而不是整条带。

entries.definition: The zone between high and low water and the shallow sea beyond it; it is more strictly tidal than the planning term.
entries.definitionCN: 高潮线与低潮线之间及以外浅海的区域；它比规划术语更严格地限于潮汐范围。

entries.definition: The belt along a river; it shares the belt idea but not the coastal setting, and its root is Latin ripa 'bank'.
entries.definitionCN: 沿河的带状地带；它与「带」的观念相同，却不是海岸环境，词根是拉丁 ripa「河岸」。

entries.definition: The sea area extending two hundred nautical miles from the coast; it is a maritime jurisdiction, not the land-sea strip.
entries.definitionCN: 从海岸向外延伸二百海里的海域；它是海洋管辖范围，不是陆海交界带。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Greek and Latin parts, real planning collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊与拉丁构件、真实规划搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Zone comes from Greek zōnē, a belt, and geographers still use it for belts of climate.
normal.cn: zone 出自希腊 zōnē「带」，地理学家至今用它指气候带。

normal.en: Coastal says where; zone says it is a belt with limits.
normal.cn: coastal 说明在哪里，zone 说明它是一条有边界的带。

normal.en: Coastal zone management is the standard policy phrase for the strip.
normal.cn: 海岸带管理是这条带的标准政策说法。

normal.en: The zone runs from the dune crest through the beach into the shallow sea.
normal.cn: 这条带从沙丘脊线穿过海滩，一直伸进浅海。

normal.en: The same belt is habitat, jurisdiction and building land at once.
normal.cn: 同一条带同时是生境、管辖范围与建设用地。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon laid over the coast, one half on land and one half in water.
abstract.cn: 想象一条缎带铺在海岸上，一半在陆地，一半在水里。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting room where the sea and the land negotiate through tides.
abstract.cn: 想象一间会议室，海与陆通过潮汐谈判。

abstract.en: Picture a legal line drawn in the sand that the tide ignores twice a day.
abstract.cn: 想象沙上画出的法定界线，而潮汐每天两次无视它。

examples.en: Integrated coastal zone management brings agencies to one table.
examples.cn: 海岸带综合管理把各机构拉到同一张桌前。

examples.en: The coastal zone supports both fisheries and tourism.
examples.cn: 海岸带同时支撑渔业与旅游业。

examples.en: Rising seas are squeezing the coastal zone from both sides.
examples.cn: 上升的海面从两侧挤压海岸带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「coastal（海岸的）+ zone（带）」——沿着海岸划出的一条带 → 海岸带

root: 拉丁 costa「肋骨、侧边」→ 古法语 coste「岸」→ 英语 coast + -al → coastal；拉丁 zona「带」← 希腊 zōnē「腰带」。两词在二十世纪海岸管理立法中合为 coastal zone。costa 与 zōnē 的更深来源均不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one belt: a physical strip, a tidal reach, an ecotone, a legal zone, a development corridor, a settled belt, a landform unit, and finally any interface between two systems.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一条「带」展开：物理地带、潮汐岸段、生态过渡带、法定管理区、开发走廊、聚居带、地貌单元，最后引申为任何两个系统之间的接口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow ribbon from the dune crest to the shallow sea, with beach, marsh and water laid side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从沙丘脊线延伸到浅海的窄带，海滩、盐沼与浅水并排铺开。

branches.en: TIDE CREATES HABITAT: daily flooding mixes salt and fresh water and makes the strip an ecotone.
branches.cn: 潮汐造出生境：每日淹水混合盐淡水，使这条带成为生态过渡带。

branches.en: GEOMORPHOLOGY: beach, dune, cliff and marsh form one sediment-linked landform system.
branches.cn: 地貌系统：海滩、沙丘、崖壁与盐沼组成一个共享沉积物的地貌体系。

branches.en: LAW ENABLES DEVELOPMENT: a mapped boundary makes permits, setbacks and ports possible.
branches.cn: 法律促成开发：画定的边界使许可、退让线与港口成为可能。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND ECONOMY: the settled belt is a market in its own right.
branches.cn: 人口与经济：这条聚居带本身就是一片市场。

branches.en: INTERFACE METAPHOR: any meeting place of two systems can borrow the coastal image.
branches.cn: 接口比喻：任何两个系统的交汇处都能借用海岸的意象。

intro.en: Coastal zone is a two-part technical compound: an adjective of place plus a noun of bounded area. Both parts are borrowed, but both are fully productive in English.
intro.cn: coastal zone 是两部分构成的技术复合词：一个表示地点的形容词，加一个表示有界区域的名词。两部分都是借词，但在英语中都能产。

latinIntro.en: Costa gives coast and coastal; zona gives zone, zoning and zonation. The Greek belt word reached English through Latin, so the Latin layer carries it.
latinIntro.cn: costa 提供 coast 与 coastal；zona 提供 zone、zoning 与 zonation。希腊的「带」词经拉丁进入英语，因此由拉丁层承载。

items.structure: Latin costa via Old French coste
items.example: The coast is low and sandy here.
Coastal wetlands filter river water.
The map marks a flood zone.

items.meaning: division of land into use districts
items.meaningCN: 把土地划分为用途分区
items.example: Zoning keeps industry off the dune.
items.exampleCN: 分区规划让工业远离沙丘。

items.example: Zonation is clear on rocky shores.
items.exampleCN: 岩岸上的成带分布很清楚。

items.example: The coastal zone is mapped every decade.
items.exampleCN: 海岸带每十年重绘一次。

items.example: Coastal-zone rules limit new hotels.
items.exampleCN: 海岸带规定限制新建旅馆。

items.meaning: the shallow water close to the shore
items.example: Nearshore currents move the sand.

items.meaning: a required distance from the water
items.example: A setback keeps houses off the active beach.
items.exampleCN: 退让线让房屋避开活动海滩。

definition_zh: 主权；国家握有的最高权力；主权国家的地位；对某片领土的管辖权；个人自主；神对历史的支配
definition_en: supreme authority within a state, the status of being an independent state, jurisdiction over territory, and by extension personal autonomy or divine rule
core_image: 一把钥匙插在国界碑的锁孔里，钥匙柄铸成王冠的形状
scene: 国界碑旁的石台上放着一把钥匙，钥匙柄铸成王冠形状，两侧的哨兵站得笔直。 The treaty recognised the new state's sovereignty over the whole valley.
sceneCN: 这里 sovereignty 指「国家握有的最高权力」（第 1 个义项：对内最高、对外不受支配的统治权）；句意为条约承认这个新国家对整个山谷拥有主权。可辨识物件：国界碑、钥匙、王冠形钥匙柄、哨兵、条约文本。

pos.zh: 主权；最高统治权；主权国家地位；个人自主（多作不可数）

forms.label: 复数（指多项主权，较少用）

derivatives.zh: sovereignty 去掉 -ty 回溯到古法语 soverain → 君主、握有主权的，语义由抽象权力回到握权者
sovereign + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以最高权力方式地
古法语 suserain（无插入 g 的形式）→ 宗主，语义由完全主权降为对他国的宗主权
suzerain + -ty（状态后缀）→ 宗主权，语义为主权的部分让渡

senses.title: Supreme authority within a state
senses.definition: the full power to make and enforce law within a territory, subject to no higher domestic authority
senses.definitionCN: 在一国领土内制定与执行法律的完整权力，不受更高的国内权威约束
senses.example: The treaty recognised the new state's sovereignty over the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 条约承认这个新国家对整个山谷拥有主权。
senses.why: The word names the quality of being sovereign, and sovereign meant 'above' others in the hierarchy of power.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指「处于主权者地位」的性质，而 sovereign 本指在权力等级中「居于其上」。

senses.title: The status of an independent state
senses.definition: the recognised standing of a state as independent and equal in international law
senses.definitionCN: 一国在国际法上被视为独立且平等的地位
senses.example: Recognition of sovereignty came only after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 主权地位直到战后才得到承认。
senses.why: In international law sovereignty is a status that other states grant, not merely a fact of power.
senses.whyCN: 在国际法中，主权是其他国家给予的地位，而不只是权力事实。

senses.title: Jurisdiction over a particular territory
senses.definition: the legal right to govern a specific area, often disputed between states
senses.definitionCN: 治理特定地区的法律权利，常在国家间发生争议
senses.example: The court disputed sovereignty over the islands.
senses.exampleCN: 法院对这些岛屿的主权归属存在争议。
senses.why: Supreme power has to be located somewhere, so the word is often used with 'over' plus a named place.
senses.whyCN: 最高权力必须落在某处，因此这个词常与 over 加具体地名连用。

senses.title: The authority of a monarch
senses.definition: the personal right of a king or queen to rule, in the older constitutional order
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的宪政秩序中，国王或女王个人拥有的统治权利
senses.example: In the old order, sovereignty belonged to the crown alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧秩序中，主权只属于王冠。
senses.why: Before states were impersonal, sovereignty was the ruler's own possession, and that historical layer remains in the word.
senses.whyCN: 在国家尚未非人格化之前，主权是统治者本人的财产，这一历史层仍留在词中。

senses.title: Freedom from outside control
senses.definition: the ability of a people or state to decide its own affairs without foreign direction
senses.definitionCN: 一个民族或国家不受外国指挥而自决事务的能力
senses.example: The movement demanded sovereignty in economic policy.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动要求在经济政策上拥有自主权。
senses.why: If supreme authority is not held abroad, then autonomy at home is the same idea seen from the border.
senses.whyCN: 既然最高权力不在国外，那么国内自主就是从边界那一侧看到的同一观念。

senses.title: Supreme power as a theoretical concept
senses.titleCN: 政治理论中的最高权力概念
senses.definition: the abstract location of final law-making authority in a political community
senses.definitionCN: 政治共同体中最终立法权威的抽象归属
senses.example: Bodin placed sovereignty in the office that makes law.
senses.exampleCN: 博丹把主权放在制定法律的职位上。
senses.why: Political theory turned a practical power into an analytic question: where does final authority sit?
senses.whyCN: 政治理论把一种实际权力转为分析问题：最终权威究竟位于何处？

senses.title: Personal autonomy over one's own life
senses.titleCN: 对自身生活的个人自主
senses.definition: an individual's authority over their own body, choices and private sphere
senses.definitionCN: 个人对自己身体、选择与私域的权力
senses.example: She defended her sovereignty over her own body.
senses.exampleCN: 她捍卫对自己身体的自主权。
senses.why: Modern rights language applies the state's self-rule to the person, producing a moral rather than legal sovereignty.
senses.whyCN: 现代权利话语把国家的自治套用到个人身上，产生道德而非法律意义上的主权。

senses.title: Divine rule over history
senses.definition: in theology, God's supreme and unchallenged control of events
senses.definitionCN: 神学中神对万事万物至高无上的支配
senses.example: The sermon stressed God's sovereignty over history.
senses.exampleCN: 布道强调神对历史的主权。
senses.why: The word's core of unquestioned supremacy fits theology, where no earthly court can review the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 这个词「不容置疑的最高」这一核心适合神学，因为世间没有法庭能复审这位统治者。

intro.en: Sovereignty is the abstract noun of sovereign, from Old French soverain plus the suffix -ty, ultimately from Latin superanus 'chief' and super 'above'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sovereignty 是 sovereign 的抽象名词，由古法语 soverain 加后缀 -ty 构成，最终出自拉丁 superanus「首领」与 super「在上」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Super meant 'above, over'; it is the source of many English words about rank and excess.
items.cn: super 意为「在上、超过」，是许多表示等级与过量的英语词的来源。

items.en: The adjective superanus meant 'chief, superior', literally the one above the rest.
items.cn: 形容词 superanus 意为「首领的、优越的」，字面就是居于其余之上者。

items.en: Old French soverain carried the word forward, and English adopted it as sovereign with an intrusive g of uncertain origin.
items.cn: 古法语 soverain 把词向前传，英语以 sovereign 采纳，其中插入的 g 来源不确定。

items.en: The French abstract ending -té, from Latin -tas, made sovereignty the name of the quality or office.
items.cn: 法语抽象词尾 -té（源自拉丁 -tas）使 sovereignty 成为性质或职位的名称。

items.en: From Bodin in the sixteenth century, sovereignty became the technical term for the final law-making power in a state.
items.cn: 自十六世纪的博丹起，主权成为指国家最终立法权力的技术术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): no exact first English citation is established, and the intrusive g in sovereign has never been fully explained; forms without it survive in suzerain.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：确切的最早英语书证未有定论；sovereign 中插入的 g 从未得到完满解释，不带 g 的形式保存在 suzerain 中。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same superanus stock or accidental neighbours; group two holds words for self-rule and supreme authority.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 superanus 词干或偶然相邻的形式；第二组是表示自治与最高权威的词。

entries.definition: The ruler or the adjective 'supreme'; sovereignty is the abstract quality or office.
entries.definitionCN: 统治者或形容词「最高的」；sovereignty 是抽象性质或职位。

entries.definition: From the same Old French word without the inserted g: a lord who controls another state's foreign affairs while leaving it internally self-governing.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古法语而不带插入的 g：控制他国外交、却让其内部自治的宗主。

entries.definition: From Latin superior, the comparative of super: higher in rank. It shares the 'above' root but not the legal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 superior，super 的比较级：等级更高。共享「在上」词根，但无法律义。

entries.definition: From superbus 'proud, magnificent': excellent. It looks like a relative but the meaning took a different path.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 superbus「骄傲、壮丽」：极好的。看似同族，但语义走了另一条路。

entries.definition: The right of a group to govern itself; it is often a limited or delegated form of sovereignty.
entries.definitionCN: 一个群体自我治理的权利；常为主权的有限或授让形式。

entries.definition: Freedom from external rule; it names the fact of being free, while sovereignty names the legal authority.
entries.definitionCN: 不受外部统治；指自由这一事实，而 sovereignty 指法律权威。

entries.definition: The right to give orders or make decisions; it need not be supreme or territorial.
entries.definitionCN: 发令或决策的权利；不必是最高的，也不必与领土相关。

entries.definition: Territory under one government, or the power to rule it; sovereignty is the authority, dominion often the land.
entries.definitionCN: 受同一政府管辖的领土，或其统治权；sovereignty 侧重权威，dominion 常指土地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: super 'above' + -anus 'belonging to' + -ty 'state': the state of being above all rivals.
normal.cn: super「在上」+ -anus「属于」+ -ty「状态」：居于所有对手之上的状态。

normal.en: The family runs sovereign, sovereignty, sovereignly, suzerain, suzerainty.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sovereign、sovereignty、sovereignly、suzerain、suzerainty。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: national sovereignty, territorial sovereignty, sovereignty over the islands.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：国家主权、领土主权、对这些岛屿的主权。

normal.en: The g in sovereign is unexplained; suzerain keeps the older shape without it.
normal.cn: sovereign 中的 g 无法解释；suzerain 保留了不带 g 的较早形态。

normal.en: Bodin turned sovereignty into the technical question of where final law-making power sits.
normal.cn: 博丹把主权变成「最终立法权位于何处」的技术问题。

abstract.en: Picture a key that opens a border gate and cannot be copied abroad.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能打开国门，却无法在境外复制。

abstract.en: Picture a state with no higher court to appeal to.
abstract.cn: 想象一个国家，没有更高的法庭可以上诉。

abstract.en: Picture a person drawing a line around their own life and calling it a border.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在自己生活周围画一条线，称它为边界。

examples.en: The constitution places sovereignty in the people rather than in a crown.
examples.cn: 宪法把主权放在人民而非王冠手中。

examples.en: Talks over sovereignty stalled for a decade.
examples.cn: 关于主权的谈判停滞了十年。

examples.en: Theologians write about sovereignty without any reference to parliaments.
examples.cn: 神学家谈主权时完全不提议会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sovereign」君主 + 「ty」状态——君主所握的那种最高权 → 主权

root: 古法语 soverain「首领」+ -ty（状态后缀，源自拉丁 -tas）；soverain 出自通俗拉丁 superanus「居上者」，再上溯 super「在上」。英语 sovereignty。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one claim to be above all rivals: it can sit in a state, a status, a territory, a throne, a people, a theory, a person or a god.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「居于所有对手之上」的主张展开：它可以落在国家、地位、领土、王座、人民、理论、个人或神身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crown-shaped key turning in the lock of a border stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把王冠形钥匙在国界碑的锁孔中转动。

branches.en: POWER OVER A PLACE: supreme authority is always located somewhere.
branches.cn: 对某地的权力：最高权威总落在某处。

branches.en: THE STATUS: other states recognise independence and equality.
branches.cn: 地位：他国承认其独立与平等。

branches.en: THE CROWN: in the older order the power belonged to a person.
branches.cn: 王冠：在较早秩序中，权力属于一个人。

branches.en: SELF-RULE: a people and a person can both claim authority over their own affairs.
branches.cn: 自治：民族与个人都能主张对自身事务的权威。

branches.en: THEORY AND THEOLOGY: final authority becomes an analytic question, then an article of faith.
branches.cn: 理论与神学：最终权威先成为分析问题，再成为信仰条款。

intro.en: Sovereignty is a Latin-rooted base plus a French abstract ending, and its parts recur in English, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: sovereignty 是拉丁词根基础加法语抽象词尾，其成分在英语中反复出现，因此整个词族可按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin super and superanus give sovereign; the abstract ending -tas, through French -té, gives sovereignty; suzerain keeps the same base without the intrusive g.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 super 与 superanus 衍生 sovereign；抽象词尾 -tas 经法语 -té 构成 sovereignty；suzerain 保留同一词基而不带插入的 g。

items.example: The element also appears in superior and supervise.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 superior 与 supervise 中。

items.example: The suffix made an adjective from a preposition.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由介词构成形容词。

items.example: Superanus named the one above the rest.
items.exampleCN: superanus 指居于其余之上者。

items.example: Old French kept the sense of a lord above other lords.
items.exampleCN: 古法语保留了「众领主之上的领主」之意。

items.example: The suffix also builds royalty and loyalty.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也构成 royalty 与 loyalty。

items.example: The state defended its sovereignty.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家捍卫自己的主权。

items.example: The sovereign opened parliament.

items.structure: Old French suserain, without the intrusive g
items.meaningCN: 凌驾于他国之上的宗主
items.example: The suzerain controlled foreign policy.
Suzerainty left the province self-governing.
items.exampleCN: 宗主权让该省保持自治。

items.example: The superior officer signed the order.

definition_zh: 保险杠；缓冲器； bumper 亦指“异常丰硕的”（形容词）
definition_en: a device that absorbs shock at the front or rear of a vehicle; a bumper crop is an unusually large one
core_image: 车头的横杠，替车身先挨撞
scene: 停车场里两车轻轻一碰，横杠上留下道白痕。 The old car's bumper was dented in the collision.
sceneCN: 这里 bumper 是「保险杠」（第 1 个义项：吸收撞击的部件）；句意是旧车的保险杠在碰撞中凹了。

pos.zh: 丰盛的，异常大的（如 bumper crop 丰收）

collocations.zh: （车流）一辆接一辆，堵得水泄不通

derivatives.zh: bumper 的基础词，义为「碰撞，撞上」
由 bump 加 -y 构成，义为「颠簸的」

senses.title: A shock-absorbing bar on a vehicle

definition_zh: 假设地；假定地；从假设上说；在假定情形下
definition_en: used to say that something is being considered as an assumed possibility or imagined case, not as an established fact
core_image: 白板上画着一个标着「情形甲」的方框，里面的数字都是临时填进去的
scene: 会议开始前，主持人在白板上画出一个方框，说明框里的条件只是临时填进去的。 Hypothetically, a city of that size could survive on stored water for a month.
sceneCN: 这里指把某个情形当作假定前提来推想（第 1 个义项：假定情形）；句意为假定有那样规模的一座城市，靠储备水也许能撑一个月。场景要点：白板上的方框、临时填入的条件、被推想的结果。

pos.zh: 假设地；假定地；从假设上说

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「下置、前提」直接借入，义为「假设、假说」
由假设名词加表示「属于……的」形容词词尾构成，义为「假设的」
由假设名词加动词词尾构成，义为「提出假设」
由假设形容词与演绎形容词复合而成，义为「假说—演绎的」

senses.title: An assumed premise
senses.definition: sets up a condition that is accepted for the sake of the discussion, whether or not it is true
senses.definitionCN: 设立一个为了讨论而接受的条件，无论它是否为真
senses.example: Hypothetically, a city of that size could survive on stored water for a month.
senses.exampleCN: 假定有那样规模的一座城市，靠储备水也许能撑一个月。
senses.why: The Greek noun is a placing under, a floor laid beneath an argument; the adverb offers that floor.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语名词意为「放在下面」，即铺在论证底下的一层地板；这个副词提供的就是那层地板。

senses.title: The conversational what if
senses.definition: in speech, invites the listener to imagine a case that may never arise
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中请听者想象一个也许永远不会出现的情形
senses.example: Hypothetically, what would you do if the offer came tomorrow?
senses.exampleCN: 假设明天这个录用通知来了，你会怎么做？
senses.why: Speech uses the word as a door into an imagined room, and either side may walk back out.
senses.whyCN: 口语把这个词当作进入想象房间的一扇门，双方都可以随时退出来。

senses.title: A case constructed for argument
senses.titleCN: 为论证构造的假定案情
senses.definition: in law, logic and debate, introduces a constructed case used to test a rule
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、逻辑与辩论中，引出一个用来检验规则而构造出来的案情
senses.example: Hypothetically, a tenant who pays no rent for a year may still keep the lease.
senses.exampleCN: 假设一个房客一年不交租金，他仍可能保住租约。
senses.why: A rule is tested by inventing a case that presses on its edges.
senses.whyCN: 规则的边界是靠虚构一个压在上面的案情来检验的。

senses.title: Merely supposed, not actual
senses.definition: marks that what follows is not being claimed to exist or to have happened
senses.definitionCN: 标明所说之事并未被声称为存在或已经发生
senses.example: The company is hypothetically liable, though no claim has been filed.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在假设上负有责任，尽管还没有人提出索赔。
senses.why: The adjective carries a shadow sense: the thing is only on paper.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词带着一层阴影义：那件事只在纸面上。

senses.title: Sentence-initial framing
senses.definition: placed first to announce that the sentence is a thought experiment rather than a report
senses.definitionCN: 置于句首，宣告这句话是一场思想试验，而不是一则报告
senses.example: Hypothetically, the two effects could cancel each other out.
senses.exampleCN: 假设如此，两种效应可能会相互抵消。
senses.why: A first word tells the reader which kind of sentence this is before the content arrives.
senses.whyCN: 开头的一个词在内容到达之前，先告诉读者这是哪一种句子。

senses.title: The fixed phrase hypothetically speaking
senses.definition: in the phrase hypothetically speaking, softens a statement that might otherwise sound like a prediction
senses.definitionCN: 在「假设地说」这一固定插入语里，弱化一句本来会被听成预测的话
senses.example: Hypothetically speaking, the plan could fail within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 假设地说，这项计划可能在一年之内失败。
senses.why: The phrase marks the frame explicitly, so that the statement inside is not taken as a forecast.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把框架明明白白标出来，里面的说法就不会被当成预报。

senses.title: A scenario in a model or experiment
senses.titleCN: 模型与实验中的假设情形
senses.definition: used in science and engineering when a model is run under assumed conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在科学与工程中，当一个模型在假定条件下运行时使用
senses.example: The model was run hypothetically, with rainfall held constant for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型是在假设条件下运行的，把降雨量固定了十年。
senses.why: A model needs conditions that are set rather than observed, and the word names that setting.
senses.whyCN: 模型需要的是被设定的条件，而不是被观察到的条件，这个词命名的正是这种设定。

senses.title: Not the same as theoretically
senses.definition: the boundary sense: hypothetically sets an assumed case, which need not rest on any theory, while theoretically appeals to principles or to what a theory predicts
senses.definitionCN: 分界义：这个词只设定一个假定情形，未必依据任何理论；而「理论上」要诉诸原理或理论所预测的结果
senses.example: Hypothetically, we may assume free entry; theoretically, free entry should drive prices down.
senses.exampleCN: 假设上我们可以假定自由进入；理论上，自由进入应当压低价格。
senses.why: An assumption needs no theory; a theory makes predictions.
senses.whyCN: 假设不需要理论，而理论会作出预测。

senses.title: The elliptical hypothetically, yes
senses.definition: in short replies, grants that something would be true under the assumed case, without endorsing it as fact
senses.definitionCN: 在简短回答里承认某事在假定情形下成立，并不把它当作事实来认可
senses.example: Could the scheme work? Hypothetically, yes.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案能行吗？假设上可以。
senses.why: The reply keeps the frame alive by repeating the word instead of dropping it.
senses.whyCN: 这种回答把框架保留下来，靠重复这个词而不是把它丢掉。

intro.en: Hypothetically is hypothetical plus -ly. The family goes back to Greek hypothesis, a placing under, from hypo- under and thesis a placing, from tithenai to place. Latin took the adjective hypotheticus, and English built the rest on that stem.
intro.cn: hypothetically 是 hypothetical 加 -ly。这个词族可追到希腊语 hypothesis「放在下面」，由 hypo-「在下」与 thesis「放置」构成，动词为 tithenai「放置」。拉丁语接收了形容词 hypotheticus，英语再在这个词干上造出其余形式。

items.en: The verb meant to place or set down, and it stands behind thesis and hypothesis alike.
items.cn: 这个动词意为放置、放下，thesis 与 hypothesis 都由它而来。

items.en: The noun named a placing, and later a proposition that is put forward.
items.cn: 这个名词指放置，后来指被提出来的命题。

items.en: Hypo- under plus thesis placing made a foundation laid beneath an argument.
items.cn: hypo-「在下」加 thesis「放置」，构成铺在论证底下的基础。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective and kept the Greek sense of what is assumed.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入这个形容词，保留了希腊语「被假定」的含义。

items.en: English formed the adjective on the Latin stem; the date of its first use is only approximate.
items.cn: 英语在拉丁词干上构成这个形容词；其首次使用年代仅为约数。

items.en: The adverb added -ly to mark a statement made inside an assumed case; the exact date is uncertain.
items.cn: 副词再加 -ly，用来标记在假定情形之内说出的话；确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the placing-under stem; the second holds the theoretical and tentative words it is compared with.
note.cn: 第一组共享「放在下面」的词干；第二组是拿来与它比较的理论性与试探性说法。

entries.definition: A proposed explanation that is still to be tested.
entries.definitionCN: 指尚待检验的解释或假说。

entries.definition: Based on an assumption rather than on fact.
entries.definitionCN: 指基于假定而非事实的。

entries.definition: To put forward a hypothesis as a possible explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指提出一个假说作为可能的解释。

entries.definition: A method that derives testable predictions from a hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 指从假说推出可检验预测的方法。

entries.definition: From Greek hypo- plus krinein, to sift; it means insincerely, and its root is krinein rather than tithenai.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊语中表示「在下」与「筛分」的两个成分，意为虚伪地；其词根与「放置」无关。

entries.definition: According to theory or to what a model predicts, whether or not it happens in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指依理论或模型所预测的而言，无论实践中是否如此。

entries.definition: As an ideal principle, as opposed to actual practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为理想原则而言，与实际做法相对。

entries.definition: According to what is said or believed, often with doubt implied.
entries.definitionCN: 指据所说或据所信，常暗示怀疑。

entries.definition: As can be imagined as possible, with no assumption set up for a discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 指可以想象为可能，并未为讨论设立任何假定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Greek floor laid under an argument, the hypothesis family, and the whiteboard frame.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用希腊语里铺在论证底下的那层地板、假设词族，以及白板上的方框。

normal.en: Hypo is under and thesis is placing: a hypothesis is a floor laid under an argument.
normal.cn: 「在下」是在下，「放置」是放置：一个假设就是铺在论证底下的一层地板。

normal.en: Hypothesis, hypothetical, hypothesize and hypothetically are one family, one root, four jobs.
normal.cn: 假设、假设的、提出假设与假设地：一个词族，一个词根，四份差事。

normal.en: A whiteboard box is the word's natural habitat: conditions inside, reality outside.
normal.cn: 白板上的方框是这个词的天然栖息地：条件在框里，现实在框外。

normal.en: Hypothetically speaking is the polite way to ask what if without promising anything.
normal.cn: 「假设地说」是礼貌地问「假如」、却什么也不承诺的方式。

normal.en: The word never claims the case exists; it only asks what would follow.
normal.cn: 这个词从不声称情形真的存在，它只问「那会引出什么」。

abstract.en: An assumption is a borrowed floor on which an argument may stand.
abstract.cn: 假定是一层借来的地板，论证可以站在上面。

abstract.en: The word builds a room and leaves the door open to reality.
abstract.cn: 这个词搭起一个房间，却把门留给现实。

abstract.en: What is only supposed can be powerful and still be false.
abstract.cn: 只是被假定的东西，可以很有力，也仍然是假的。

examples.en: Hypothetically, a smaller dose might produce the same effect.
examples.cn: 假设如此，较小的剂量也许能产生同样的效果。

examples.en: Hypothetically speaking, the two policies could be combined.
examples.cn: 假设地说，这两项政策是可以合并的。

examples.en: The engineers tested the design hypothetically before building a prototype.
examples.cn: 工程师在造出样机之前，先在假设条件下检验了这个设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「海波塞提克理」——先在海面上放一个假设的盒子，再看里面会怎样：假设地

root: 希腊语 tithenai「放置」→ thesis「放置、命题」→ hypo-（在下）+ thesis 构成 hypothesis「放在下面的前提」→ 拉丁语 hypotheticus → 英语 hypothetical，再加副词词尾构成。直接来源清楚；副词首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses differ by the frame being set up: an assumed premise, a spoken what if, a case built for argument, a merely supposed state, the sentence-initial frame, the fixed phrase, a model scenario, the boundary against theoretically, and the short reply.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项按所设的框架分开：假定前提、口语的「假如」、为论证构造的案情、只是纸面上的假定、句首设定、固定插入语、模型情形、与「理论上」的分界，以及简短回答。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whiteboard box labelled CASE A, its figures filled in only for the discussion.
core.cn: 核心意象：白板上一个标着「情形甲」的方框，框里的数字只为这次讨论临时填上。

branches.en: THE ASSUMED PREMISE: a condition accepted, whether it stands at the head of the sentence or inside it.
branches.cn: 假定前提：一个被接受的条件，无论它放在句首还是句中。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN FRAME: an imagined case in conversation, and the short reply that keeps it alive.
branches.cn: 口语框架：对话里想象的情形，以及让这个框架继续成立的简短回答。

branches.en: THE CONSTRUCTED CASE: one built to test a rule, one run inside a model.
branches.cn: 构造的案情：一个用来检验规则，一个在模型里运行。

branches.en: THE MARKED SUPPOSITION: only on paper, and openly labelled by the fixed phrase.
branches.cn: 标明了的假定：只在纸面上，并由固定插入语公开标出。

branches.en: THE BOUNDARY: an assumption needs no theory, while a theory makes predictions.
branches.cn: 分界：假设不需要理论，而理论会作出预测。

intro.en: Hypothetically is a Greek noun of placing, filtered through Latin, wearing an English adjective ending and an adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个经拉丁语过滤的希腊「放置」名词，套着英语的形容词词尾与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies hypo-, thesis and tithenai; hypothesis entered Latin, and the adjective hypotheticus became the English stem.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了 hypo-、thesis 与 tithenai；hypothesis 进入拉丁语，形容词 hypotheticus 则成为英语的词干。

items.example: It places the premise beneath the argument.
items.exampleCN: 它把前提放在论证的下面。

items.example: The noun names what is set down.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被放下的东西。

items.example: The verb is the action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词背后的动作。

items.meaning: a premise laid under an argument
items.example: The word enters learned English through Latin.
items.exampleCN: 这个词经拉丁语进入学术英语。

items.example: Latin gives English the adjective stem.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语给英语提供了形容词词干。

items.example: English adds its own adjective ending to the stem.
items.exampleCN: 英语在词干上加了自身的形容词词尾。

items.example: It forms the adjective from the Greek noun.
items.exampleCN: 它由希腊名词构成形容词。

items.example: It forms hypothesize, to put forward a hypothesis.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 hypothesize，即提出假设。

items.example: It forms the adverb of assumed cases.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示假定情形的副词。

latinEntries.meaning: a premise laid under an argument

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语「下置、前提」经拉丁语借入，义为「假设」
由假设名词加「属于……的」形容词词尾构成，义为「假设的」
由假设名词加动词词尾构成，义为「提出假设」
由假设形容词与演绎形容词复合而成，义为「假说—演绎的」

definition_zh: 证伪；证明为假；伪造；篡改（记录、数据、账目）；（哲学）可证伪性方法中的反证环节
definition_en: the act of showing that a statement or theory is false, or of making a document or record false
core_image: 一支笔把文件上原本的数字划掉，改写成另一个数字，墨迹还压在纸面上
scene: 档案馆里有人把原始记录的年份悄悄改早，后来的研究者用同位素检测发现了这处改动。 The historian exposed a falsification of the archive record that had stood for sixty years.
sceneCN: 这里指对记录、数据的篡改（第 3 个义项：伪造、篡改）；句意为这位历史学家揭穿了一处冒充了六十年的档案篡改。场景图取象：文件上的数字被划掉改写。

pos.zh: 伪造；篡改（文件、数据、账目）
（哲学）证伪；反证的一次具体操作

derivatives.zh: 证伪；伪造（由「假」与「做」两个拉丁词根合成，字面即「使之为假」）
可证伪的（加表示「能够被……」的形容词后缀，指一种说法能被事实推翻）
证伪者；伪造者（加表示「施动者」的名词后缀，兼指做实验推翻理论与造假两种人）
虚假；不实（由「假」的形容词加表示「性质」的名词后缀构成）
谎言；虚假陈述（英语本族语复合词，指不实之事）
证伪主义（在证伪后加表示「学说」的后缀，指以能否被推翻来判断科学性的主张）

senses.title: Showing a claim is false
senses.definition: the act of proving that a statement, belief or theory is false
senses.definitionCN: 证明一个说法、信念或理论为假的行为
senses.example: The falsification of the rumour took only one document.
senses.exampleCN: 推翻那个传闻只用了一份文件。
senses.why: The word is built as 'making false', and the oldest sense is exactly that: bringing a claim down.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「使之为假」构成，最古老的义项正就是这个：把一种说法打翻。

senses.title: The test that could fail
senses.definition: in the philosophy of science, a test so framed that a negative result would count against the theory
senses.definitionCN: 在科学哲学中，设计得使否定结果足以打击该理论的一次检验
senses.example: Popper made falsification the mark of a scientific claim.
senses.exampleCN: 波普尔把证伪立为科学主张的标志。
senses.why: A theory that cannot lose is not being tested; the power to be shown false is what makes a test real.
senses.whyCN: 不会输的理论并没有受检；能被证明为假的力量，才让检验成其为检验。

senses.title: Doctoring a record
senses.definition: the deliberate alteration of a document, data set or account so that it misrepresents the facts
senses.definitionCN: 故意改动文件、数据集或账目，使其歪曲事实
senses.example: The audit found falsification of three quarterly reports.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现三份季度报告被篡改。
senses.why: The same verb that means proving false also means making false, and paperwork is where the second sense lives.
senses.whyCN: 既表示「证明为假」又表示「使之为假」的同一个动词，第二层意思就落在纸面上。

senses.title: A refuting instance
senses.definition: a single observation or case that contradicts a general statement and thereby disproves it
senses.definitionCN: 与一般性陈述相抵触、从而推翻它的一条观察或事例
senses.example: One falsification is enough to sink a universal claim.
senses.exampleCN: 一条反证就足以推翻一个全称主张。
senses.why: Universal claims promise everything without exception, so one exception makes the promise false.
senses.whyCN: 全称主张承诺无一例外，因此一个例外就让这承诺为假。

senses.title: Forgery of a signature
senses.definition: the forging of a signature, document or certificate so that it appears genuine
senses.definitionCN: 伪造签名、文件或证书，使其看起来像真品
senses.example: Falsification of a passport is a criminal offence.
senses.exampleCN: 伪造护照是刑事犯罪。
senses.why: Forgery makes a false thing pass as true, which is the 'making false' branch in its legal form.
senses.whyCN: 伪造让假东西冒充真东西，这是「使之为假」一脉在法律上的形态。

senses.title: Research misconduct
senses.definition: the fabrication or manipulation of research data, images or results
senses.definitionCN: 编造或操纵研究数据、图像或结果
senses.example: The journal retracted the paper after evidence of falsification.
senses.exampleCN: 有造假证据后，期刊撤下了那篇论文。
senses.why: Modern universities separate honest error from falsification, because only the second is misconduct.
senses.whyCN: 现代大学把诚实的错误与造假分开，因为只有后者才算不端。

senses.title: False accounting
senses.definition: the falsification of financial accounts, invoices or tax records
senses.definitionCN: 对财务账目、发票或税务记录的作假
senses.example: He was charged with falsification of company accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控对公司账目作假。
senses.why: Law names the offence after the act, and accounts are the documents most often made false.
senses.whyCN: 法律以动作命名罪名，而账目是最常被做假的文件。

senses.title: The state of being disproved
senses.definition: the condition of a statement that has been shown to be false
senses.definitionCN: 某一说法已被证明为假的状态
senses.example: The falsification of that model came from its own predictions.
senses.exampleCN: 那个模型是被它自己的预测推翻的。
senses.why: The noun can name the outcome as well as the act, so a theory can be said to suffer falsification.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也能指结果而非动作，所以说一个理论遭到证伪。

senses.title: A counterfeit copy
senses.definition: a copy or imitation made to be taken for the genuine article
senses.definitionCN: 被做出来冒充真品的复制件或仿制品
senses.example: The museum rejected the painting as a falsification.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆认定这幅画是赝品而拒收。
senses.why: A false copy is a thing made false in the literal sense, and the word carries that older weight.
senses.whyCN: 假画就是字面意义上被做假的东西，这个词还带着那层旧有的分量。

intro.en: Falsification joins Latin falsus 'false' with facere 'to make'. Both elements are well attested; the only uncertain point is how early the 'forgery' sense appears in English.
intro.cn: falsification 把拉丁语 falsus「假」与 facere「做」合在一起。两个构件都有充分记录，唯一不确定的是「伪造」这一义项在英语中出现得有多早。

items.en: Falsus meant false or deceptive and came from fallere, to deceive, which also stands behind fail, fault and fallacy.
items.cn: falsus 意为虚假的、骗人的，出自 fallere「欺骗」，fail、fault 与 fallacy 也源于此。

items.en: Fallere first described a trick or a slip, and its family spreads across failure, default and fallible.
items.cn: fallere 最初描述欺骗或失足，其词族延伸到 failure、default 与 fallible。

items.en: The second element, to make, turns the adjective into a verb of producing a state: to make false.
items.cn: 第二个构件意为做、造，把形容词变成制造某种状态的动词：使之为假。

items.en: Late Latin falsificare meant to make false or to counterfeit, a word used of coins and documents as well as arguments.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 falsificare 意为使假或伪造，既用于钱币与文件，也用于论证。

items.en: English took the noun in the sixteenth century; the exact date of its first use in the forgery sense is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个名词；它首次用于「伪造」义的确切年代不确定。

items.en: In the 1930s Karl Popper made falsification the test of scientific status, and the word became a term of method.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十年代，波普尔把证伪立为科学资格的检验，这个词于是成了方法论术语。

note.en: The first group shares the false-making root or only looks close; the second group holds the neighbouring acts that are often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「使假」词根，或只是字形相近；第二组是常与之混淆的邻近行为。

entries.definition: The verb: to prove false or to make a record false.
entries.definitionCN: 动词：证明为假，或把记录做假。

entries.definition: Able to be shown false, the quality Popper demanded of a theory.
entries.definitionCN: 能被证明为假的，正是波普尔对理论的要求。

entries.definition: The plain adjective of untruth, from the same Latin source.
entries.definitionCN: 最朴素的「假」的形容词，来自同一拉丁语来源。

entries.definition: A mistaken argument that looks convincing; it shares fallere but not facere.
entries.definitionCN: 看似有理实则错误的论证；共享「欺骗」词根，不含「做」。

entries.definition: Making a process easier; the ending matches but the root means easy.
entries.definitionCN: 使过程更容易；词尾相同，词根却意为容易。

entries.definition: The act of proving an argument or claim wrong by evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 用证据证明某一论证或主张有误。

entries.definition: Evidence that a claim is false, the plain noun for a negative result.
entries.definitionCN: 证明主张为假的证据，最朴素的否定结果之名。

entries.definition: A false document, signature or object made to pass as genuine.
entries.definitionCN: 为冒充真品而造的假文件、假签名或假器物。

entries.definition: Inventing data or a story; falsification alters what exists, fabrication creates what does not.
entries.definitionCN: 编造数据或故事；造假改动已有之物，编造则凭空造出。

entries.definition: Publicly exposing a false claim, usually in journalism rather than in method.
entries.definitionCN: 公开揭穿虚假说法，多见于新闻而非方法论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real false-making root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「使假」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Falsus is false and facere is make, so falsification is literally the making false of something.
normal.cn: 前者为假，后者为做，字面就是把某物做成假的。

normal.en: Fallere, to deceive, also gives fail, fault and fallacy, so the whole family smells of a slip.
normal.cn: 表示欺骗的 fallere 还给出 fail、fault 与 fallacy，整个词族都带着失足的气味。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: falsification of data, falsification of records, falsification test.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：数据篡改、伪造记录、证伪检验。

normal.en: In science the word is honourable: a theory earns trust by surviving attempts at falsification.
normal.cn: 在科学里这个词是体面的：理论靠挺过证伪的尝试而赢得信任。

normal.en: In paperwork the same word is a crime: falsification of accounts and of passports.
normal.cn: 在文书里同一个词是罪名：账目作假与伪造护照。

abstract.en: Falsification is the only honest way a theory can be wrong in public.
abstract.cn: 证伪是一个理论能在公开场合出错的唯一体面方式。

abstract.en: A claim that nothing could ever contradict is not strong; it is simply out of reach.
abstract.cn: 任何东西都无法反驳的说法并不强大，只是够不着。

abstract.en: Making a record false is a small war on memory, since the paper was supposed to remember for us.
abstract.cn: 把记录做假，是对记忆发动的一场小战争，因为纸本来该替我们记住。

examples.en: The falsification of the original minutes changed the whole case.
examples.cn: 原始会议记录被篡改，整个案子都变了。

examples.en: Popper treated falsification as the dividing line of science.
examples.cn: 波普尔把证伪当作科学的分界线。

examples.en: A single falsification ended the belief in that remedy.
examples.cn: 一条反证终结了人们对那种疗法的相信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「佛西菲克申」——把「假」做出来，划掉原字改写：证伪、伪造

root: 晚期拉丁语 falsificare「使假、伪造」← 拉丁语 falsus「假」＋ facere「做」，falsus 出自 fallere「欺骗」，同族有 fail、fault、fallacy、false。十六世纪进入英语；证伪作为科学方法术语由波普尔在二十世纪三十年代确立。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from proving a claim false, through a test that could fail, to doctored records, a single counterexample, a forged signature, research misconduct, false accounts, the state of being disproved, and a counterfeit copy.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「证明说法为假」出发，经过可能失败的一次检验，到篡改记录、一条反证、伪造签名、科研造假、账目作假、被推翻的状态，最后是冒充真品的仿件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number on a page crossed out and rewritten, with the old ink still under the new.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸上的数字被划掉改写，旧的墨迹还压在新字下面。

branches.en: THE CLAIM BROUGHT DOWN: the act of proving a statement false, and the state it is left in.
branches.cn: 被打翻的主张：证明说法为假的动作，以及它被留下时的状态。

branches.en: THE TEST AND THE INSTANCE: a planned attempt that could fail, and the single case that does the failing.
branches.cn: 检验与实例：一次可能失败的设计，以及真正造成失败的那一个事例。

branches.en: THE DOCTORED PAPER: records and accounts altered so that they misstate the facts.
branches.cn: 被改动的纸面：记录与账目被改动，从而歪曲事实。

branches.en: THE FALSE THING: a forged signature or a copy passed off as the genuine article.
branches.cn: 假东西：伪造的签名，或被当作真品递出的仿件。

branches.en: THE MISCONDUCT: research data invented or manipulated, which the word separates from honest error.
branches.cn: 不端行为：研究数据被编造或操纵，这个词把它与诚实的错误分开。

intro.en: Falsification is built from the Latin words for false and make, and the same endings recur across English.
intro.cn: falsification 由拉丁语「假」与「做」两个词构成，同样的词尾在英语中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin falsus and facere are the sources, with the noun ending through Late Latin -ficatio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falsus 与 facere 是来源，名词词尾经由晚期拉丁语的 -ficatio 而来。

items.example: The noun names both the act and the false result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指动作，也指假的结果。

items.example: It is the past participle of the verb to deceive.
items.exampleCN: 它是表示欺骗的动词的过去分词。

items.example: It supplies the -fication ending.
It builds amplification, classification and falsification.
items.exampleCN: 它构成放大、分类与证伪等词。

items.example: It builds falsify, verify and simplify.
items.exampleCN: 它构成证伪、核实与简化。

items.example: The adjective keeps the oldest layer of meaning.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留最古老的一层意思。

items.example: The adjective is the key term of Popper's method.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是波普尔方法的关键词。

items.example: The ending marks the person, honest or not.
items.exampleCN: 词尾标出人，无论诚实与否。

items.example: The noun names the property rather than the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指性质而非动作。

latinEntries.example: Medieval Latin falsificare means to make false or to counterfeit.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语 falsificare 意为使假、伪造。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective falsus (false), participle of fallere
latinEntries.example: Latin falsus means false, from fallere, to deceive.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 falsus 意为假的，出自 fallere（欺骗）。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb facere (fac-, factum; to make)
latinEntries.example: Latin facere supplies the making of the compound.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 facere 提供该复合词中「造」的部分。

definition_zh: 突然地；意外地；唐突地；生硬地；陡然地；猛然地；不连贯地；骤发地
definition_en: in a sudden, curt, steep, jerky, or disconnected manner, with no transition before or after
core_image: 一段正在播放的录音被人直接按下停止键，声音在一个字中间被切断。
scene: 这里指「突然地」。 She stopped speaking abruptly when she saw who had entered.
sceneCN: 这里 abruptly 是「突然地、毫无过渡地」（第 1 个义项），并与第 2 个义项“生硬”相邻；句意：一看见进来的是谁，她就突然住口。场景：半句悬在空中、门口的人影、旁人的目光。

senses.title: Suddenly and without warning
senses.definition: in a way that happens quickly and unexpectedly, leaving no time to react
senses.definitionCN: 发生得又快又意外，来不及反应
senses.example: The storm arrived abruptly, before the boats could return.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴来得突然，船还没来得及回港。
senses.why: The adverb adds manner to the adjective: the break is not only present, it is how the event entered the scene.
senses.whyCN: 副词给形容词加了“方式”：断裂不仅存在，而且事件就是以这种方式闯入场景的。

senses.title: Curtly and unfriendlily
senses.titleCN: 生硬：把话说到一半就收回
senses.definition: in a short, sharp way that seems rude or dismissive
senses.definitionCN: 以简短、尖锐的方式，显得无礼或轻慢
senses.example: He answered abruptly and turned back to his paper.
senses.exampleCN: 他生硬地答了一句，又转回他的文件。
senses.why: Speaking abruptly is speaking with the social ending cut off. The adverb makes the cut audible in the voice.
senses.whyCN: 说话 abrupt，就是说话时把社交性的结尾切掉。副词让这道切口在声音里听得见。

senses.title: Steeply, with a sheer drop
senses.titleCN: 陡然地：地面直接落下去
senses.definition: with a very sharp slope, falling or rising almost vertically
senses.definitionCN: 坡度极陡，几乎垂直地下降或上升
senses.example: Beyond the ridge the ground drops abruptly to the river.
senses.exampleCN: 山脊之外，地面陡然落向河边。
senses.why: The adverb describes the shape of the fall: not a gradual slope but a line that turns down.
senses.whyCN: 副词描述“落”的形状：不是缓缓倾斜，而是一条线直接折下去。

senses.title: With a sudden stop
senses.titleCN: 猛然：正在动的东西被按住
senses.definition: stopping or halting in a single sharp movement
senses.definitionCN: 以一次短促、尖锐的动作停止
senses.example: The car braked abruptly at the crossing.
senses.exampleCN: 汽车在路口猛然刹车。
senses.why: Here the break falls on motion. What was continuous becomes a stop with no deceleration curve.
senses.whyCN: 这里的断裂落在运动上：原本连续的动作变成一次没有减速曲线的停止。

senses.title: Without a transition in a text
senses.titleCN: 不连贯地：段落之间没有桥
senses.definition: in a way that jumps from one point to another without linking words or steps
senses.definitionCN: 从一个论点跳到另一个，缺少连接词或过渡步骤
senses.example: The chapter ends abruptly, leaving the reader mid-scene.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章结束得很突兀，把读者留在场景中间。
senses.why: A text can be cut as surely as a road. The adverb marks the missing bridge between two parts.
senses.whyCN: 文本可以像道路一样被切断。副词标记的是两部分之间那座缺失的桥。

senses.title: With a sudden break in sound
senses.definition: of music or noise, stopping in the middle rather than fading or resolving
senses.definitionCN: 音乐或声响在中间停住，而不是渐弱或收束
senses.example: The recording cuts off abruptly in the second verse.
senses.exampleCN: 录音在第二段歌词中戛然而止。
senses.why: Sound is the clearest place to hear abruptness: a wave that should decay is instead sliced.
senses.whyCN: 声音是听见 abrupt 最清楚的地方：本该衰减的声波，被直接切断了。

senses.title: With a sudden onset
senses.titleCN: 骤发地：症状一下子就出现
senses.definition: beginning suddenly rather than building up, used of illnesses and attacks
senses.definitionCN: 一开始就很急，而非逐渐累积，用于疾病与发作
senses.example: The headache began abruptly during the lecture.
senses.exampleCN: 头痛在讲座进行中骤然开始。
senses.why: Medical writing uses the adverb to place the start of a symptom precisely: the onset line jumps.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作里，这个副词用来精确放置症状的起点：起病线是跳上去的。

senses.title: In a cut-off or truncated way
senses.titleCN: 被截断地：话没说完就没了
senses.definition: ending before the expected completion, as if the remaining part were removed
senses.definitionCN: 在预期完成之前就结束，好像剩下的部分被移除
senses.example: The announcement was cut off abruptly by static.
senses.exampleCN: 公告被静电噪声突然截断。
senses.why: Truncation is the purest form of the image: a line that stops, with the rest simply absent.
senses.whyCN: 截断是这幅意象最纯粹的形式：一条线停住，其余部分干脆不存在。

intro.en: Abruptly is abrupt plus the Germanic adverb suffix -ly. The Latin part ends at abruptus; the -ly ending has its own Old English history and is not Latin at all.
intro.cn: abruptly 是 abrupt 加日耳曼语副词后缀 -ly。拉丁语部分到 abruptus 为止；-ly 有自己的古英语历史，根本不是拉丁语。

items.en: The adverb suffix came from lic, meaning body, form, or manner. -lice meant 'in the manner of', and it is the ancestor of modern -ly.
items.cn: 这个副词后缀来自 lic，意为身体、形状、方式。-lice 表示“以……的方式”，是现代 -ly 的祖先。

items.en: The same word became the adjective suffix -ly and the noun lich, a body. English -ly is Germanic, not Latin.
items.cn: 同一个词还变成形容词后缀 -ly 与名词 lich（身体）。英语的 -ly 属日耳曼语，不是拉丁语。

items.en: The suffix shortened to -li and merged with the adjective suffix, so that a word like kindly could be either adjective or adverb.
items.cn: 后缀缩短为 -li，并与形容词后缀合并，因此 kindly 这类词当时既可作形容词也可作副词。

items.en: The base word entered English in the 16c as abrupt, a past participle meaning broken off. It supplies the meaning, not the ending.
items.cn: 词基在 16 世纪以 abrupt 进入英语，是一个意为“被折断”的过去分词。它提供意义，不提供词尾。

items.en: Abrupt + -ly produces abruptly. Early uses describe physical breaks and steep ground; the manner sense follows soon after.
items.cn: abrupt 加 -ly 造出 abruptly。早期用法描述物理断裂与陡地，态度义随后出现。

items.en: The adverb becomes the standard way to modify verbs of stopping, ending, changing, and speaking, while the adjective keeps the descriptive load.
items.cn: 这个副词成为修饰 stop、end、change、speak 等动词的标准方式；形容词则继续承担描述性的分量。

note.en: The first group is the abrupt family plus one look-alike that shares rumpere but not ab-; the second separates the kinds of manner the adverb can express.
note.cn: 第一组是 abrupt 词族，外加一个共享 rumpere 却不共享 ab- 的形近词；第二组区分这个副词能表达的各种方式。

entries.definition: sudden, curt, steep, or cut short. It describes the thing; abruptly describes the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的、生硬的、陡的或被截断的；描述事物本身，而 abruptly 描述做事的方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being abrupt. It turns the adverb's manner back into a property.
entries.definitionCN: 突然、唐突的性质；把副词的方式再变回属性。

entries.definition: a sudden separation or breaking off, as of rock layers or the placenta.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的分离或断裂，如岩层或胎盘。

entries.definition: in a dishonest way. Corrupt shares Latin rumpere but takes com- 'together, completely', so it means thoroughly broken, not broken away.
entries.definitionCN: 以不诚实的方式。corrupt 共享拉丁语 rumpere，但用 com-“共同、彻底”，意为“彻底坏掉”，而非“断开离开”。

entries.definition: without warning. It is the neutral adverb of timing and says nothing about manner.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无预警地；是时间上的中性副词，不涉及态度。

entries.definition: in a blunt, slightly harsh way. It adds roughness to the curt sense.
entries.definitionCN: 以直率而略粗砺的方式；在“生硬”之上再加一层粗砺。

entries.definition: with so few words that the reply feels cut off. It is the pure manner reading of abruptly.
entries.definitionCN: 用词少到让回答像被截断；是 abruptly 纯粹的“态度”读法。

entries.definition: in a way that has a cutting edge, of tone or movement. It stresses the sting rather than the break.
entries.definitionCN: 语气或动作带锋刃；强调刺痛，而非断裂。

entries.definition: very steeply, or with reckless haste. It covers both the cliff and the timing senses.
entries.definitionCN: 极陡地，或鲁莽仓促地；同时覆盖崖壁与时间两个义项。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin abruptus 'broken off' plus Germanic -ly 'in the manner of'. The suffix is Old English, not Latin.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 abruptus“被折断的”加日耳曼语 -ly“以……方式”。这个后缀是古英语，不是拉丁语。

normal.en: Abrupt is the broken thing; abruptly is the way it breaks into the scene.
normal.cn: abrupt 是被折断的东西；abruptly 是它闯进场景的方式。

normal.en: -ly comes from Old English lic, 'body or manner', the same source as the adjective suffix.
normal.cn: -ly 来自古英语 lic“身体、方式”，与形容词后缀同源。

normal.en: A recording that stops abruptly leaves the last word hanging in the air.
normal.cn: 突然停下的录音，把最后一个词悬在空中。

normal.en: Speak abruptly and the listener hears the missing polite ending.
normal.cn: 说话 abrupt，听者听见的是那句缺失的客套结尾。

normal.en: Ground that drops abruptly is a slope that refused to slope.
normal.cn: 陡然下落的地面，是一段拒绝变斜的坡。

abstract.en: Abruptly is the adverb of unannounced endings.
abstract.cn: abruptly，是“不打招呼的结束”的副词。

abstract.en: What stops abruptly leaves a shape in the silence.
abstract.cn: 骤然停止的东西，会在寂静里留下一个形状。

abstract.en: Timing, tone, and terrain can all be cut by the same word.
abstract.cn: 时间、语气与地形，都能被同一个词切断。

examples.en: The conversation ended abruptly when the fire alarm sounded.
examples.cn: 火警响起时，谈话戛然而止。

examples.en: The land rises abruptly behind the village.
examples.cn: 村庄后面的地势陡然升高。

examples.en: He answered abruptly, then apologized for his tone.
examples.cn: 他生硬地回答，随后又为语气道歉。

dict_mnemonic.text: “额，不拉普特利”——话说到一半“额”一声就断 → abruptly 突然地、生硬地

root: 由 abrupt（← 拉丁语 abruptus，abrumpere“折断”的过去分词，ab-“离开”+ rumpere“折断”）加日耳曼语副词后缀 -ly 构成；核心是“以断裂的方式”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abruptly, one manner: something is cut rather than continued. The cut can fall on time, tone, slope, motion, text, sound, a symptom, or a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: abruptly 的八个义项只有一种方式：某事物不是延续，而是被切断。切口可以落在时间、语气、坡度、动作、文章、声音、症状或一句话上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a recording stopped mid-word, the last syllable left hanging.
core.cn: 核心意象：录音在一个词中间被按停，最后一个音节悬着。

chain: OLD ENGLISH -LICE IN THE MANNER OF

branches.en: SUDDEN TIMING: a storm and a symptom both enter without a run-up.
branches.cn: 突然的时间：风暴与症状都是没有预热就登场。

branches.en: CURT MANNER: the sentence loses its social ending and the voice sounds cut.
branches.cn: 生硬态度：句子丢掉社交性的结尾，声音听起来是被切过的。

branches.en: STEEP GROUND: the fall is a line turned down, not a curve.
branches.cn: 陡峭地面：下落是一条折下去的线，而不是曲线。

branches.en: CUTTING OFF: a brake and a truncated announcement both stop the expected continuation.
branches.cn: 截断：刹车与被截断的公告，都终止了预期的延续。

branches.en: NO TRANSITION: a text jumping between points and music sliced mid-phrase share the missing bridge.
branches.cn: 没有过渡：在论点间跳跃的文章与在乐句中切断的音乐，都缺那座桥。

intro.en: Abruptly is one of the clearest cases of a Latin stem with a Germanic suffix: abruptus supplies the meaning, -ly supplies the adverbial grammar.
intro.cn: abruptly 是“拉丁词干 + 日耳曼后缀”最清楚的例子之一：abruptus 提供意义，-ly 提供副词语法。

latinIntro.en: Latin stops at abruptus. There is no Latin -ly; the adverb ending belongs to Old English -lice. The Latin entries below are the base forms behind abrupt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语到 abruptus 为止。拉丁语没有 -ly；副词词尾属于古英语 -lice。下面的拉丁条目是 abrupt 背后的词基形式。

items.meaning: in a sudden or curt manner
items.meaningCN: 以突然或生硬的方式（形容词加 -ly 构成副词）
items.example: She left abruptly without saying goodbye.
items.exampleCN: 她没告别就突然离开了。

items.meaningCN: 被折断的；突然的；生硬的（拉丁分词作形容词）
items.example: The abrupt turn surprised the driver.
items.exampleCN: 那个急转弯让司机吃惊。

items.meaningCN: 突然或唐突的状态（-ness 构成性质名词）
items.example: The abruptness of the ending felt deliberate.
items.exampleCN: 那个结尾的突兀感像是故意的。

items.meaningCN: 突然的断裂或分离（-ion 构成名词）
items.example: The abruption left a clean face of rock.
items.exampleCN: 那次断裂留下一面平整的岩壁。

items.meaning: to cease in a single sharp movement
items.meaningCN: 以一次短促动作停止（动词搭配）
items.example: The engine stopped abruptly.

items.meaning: to finish with no closing passage
items.meaningCN: 没有收束段落就结束（动词搭配）
items.example: The letter ends abruptly in mid-sentence.
items.exampleCN: 这封信在半句处突然结束。

items.meaning: to talk in a short, unfriendly way
items.meaningCN: 以简短、不友好的方式说话（动词搭配）
items.example: He spoke abruptly to the reporters.

items.meaning: to go up with a very steep slope
items.meaningCN: 以极陡的坡度升高（动词搭配）
items.example: The cliffs rise abruptly from the sea.

items.meaning: to stop in the middle of speaking
items.meaningCN: 说到一半突然停住（短语动词搭配）
items.example: She broke off abruptly and looked away.
items.exampleCN: 她突然住口，把目光移开。

items.meaningCN: 像被切断一样终止（副词加过去分词）
items.example: The call was abruptly cut off.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 被折断的；陡的；不连贯的

definition_zh: 告诫；警告；温和的责备
definition_en: a firm but gentle warning about someone's behaviour or a coming danger
core_image: 长辈敲了敲桌子，话不重，分量却在
scene: 期末监考前，老师在讲台上扫视全班，只说了一句。 The principal gave the seniors a stern admonition about cheating.
sceneCN: 这里 admonition 是「告诫」（第 1 个义项：对行为或危险的郑重提醒）；句意为校长就作弊问题向毕业班提出严厉告诫。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「告诫；训诫」
同根形容词，义为「告诫性的；警告的」

senses.title: A firm warning
senses.definition: a warning that stresses what must not be done or what will follow
senses.definitionCN: 强调不可做何事或后果将如何的提醒
senses.example: The principal gave the seniors a stern admonition about cheating.
senses.exampleCN: 校长就作弊问题向毕业班提出严厉告诫。
senses.why: Latin monere means 'to warn'; the admonition adds a hand of care to the warning word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 monere 意为「警告」；admonition 在警告之上又加了一手关切。

senses.title: A gentle rebuke
senses.definition: a mild expression of disapproval meant to correct, not to punish
senses.definitionCN: 意在纠正而非惩罚的轻度不满
senses.example: Her late arrival earned only a quiet admonition from the coach.
senses.exampleCN: 她迟到只换来教练轻声的一句提醒。
senses.why: The same warning word softens when the goal is training rather than blame.
senses.whyCN: 当目的是培养而非苛责，同一句警告便放软了。

intro.en: Admonition comes from Latin admonitio, 'a reminding, a warning', from admonere 'to warn', from ad- plus monere 'to warn'.
intro.cn: admonition 来自拉丁语 admonitio（提醒、警告），出自 admonere（告诫），由 ad- 加 monere（警告）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *mon- meant 'to think, to remind'; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 重构词根 *mon- 意为「想、提醒」；此词根尚存疑。

items.en: monere meant 'to warn, to remind'.
items.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒」。

items.en: admonere meant 'to warn toward', to press the warning on someone.
items.cn: admonere 意为「向某人施以警告」。

items.en: admonitio named the act or words of warning.
items.cn: admonitio 指警告的行为或言辞。

items.en: English admonition entered through religious and moral writing and stays formal.
items.cn: 英语 admonition 经宗教与道德写作进入，至今保持书面色彩。

note.en: The first group gathers the monere family; the second gathers words for warning and rebuke.
note.cn: 第一组收 monere 词族；第二组收表示警告与责备的词。

entries.definition: The parent verb, to warn or mildly rebuke.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告诫」，本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: The adjective for a warning look or tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「告诫性的」。

entries.definition: One who reminds and watches; same root turned technical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「监视器；监督者」；同根转为技术义。

entries.definition: A warning to take care.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小心；警告」。

entries.definition: A formal expression of disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「训斥」，分量更重。

entries.definition: Urging toward action rather than away from it.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「劝诫」，方向是劝进。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the warn root monere and the exam scene; the abstract hooks picture a finger tapped on the desk.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「警告」词根 monere 与考试场景；抽象记忆点想象在桌上轻敲的手指。

normal.en: Admonition is admonish plus -ition.
normal.cn: admonition 是 admonish 加 -ition。

normal.en: A word of admonition is the common phrase.
normal.cn: a word of admonition 是常用表达。

normal.en: Monitor shares the root: one who watches and warns.
normal.cn: monitor 同根：看守并提醒的人。

normal.en: It is gentler than reprimand.
normal.cn: 它比 reprimand 温和。

normal.en: The word is formal and written.
normal.cn: 这个词正式且多用于书面。

abstract.en: Picture a knuckle tapping twice on the desk.
abstract.cn: 想象指节在桌上轻敲两下。

abstract.en: Picture a raised eyebrow that says enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一个扬起的眉毛说明一切。

abstract.en: Picture a signpost before a narrow bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象窄桥前的路牌。

examples.en: The principal gave the seniors a stern admonition about cheating.
examples.cn: 校长就作弊问题向毕业班提出严厉告诫。

examples.en: Her late arrival earned only a quiet admonition from the coach.
examples.cn: 她迟到只换来教练轻声的一句提醒。

examples.en: The manual ends with an admonition to check the fuse first.
examples.cn: 手册结尾告诫要先检查保险丝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的摸你神」——额头摸摸你的神色，提醒你注意，就是告诫。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ monere（警告）→ admonere（告诫）→ admonitio（警告）；核心义是「带着关切压向对方的提醒」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a firm warning, to a gentle rebuke meant to correct.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从郑重的警告，走到意在纠正的温和责备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger tapped on the desk

definition_zh: 使过时；使陈旧；废弃
definition_en: to make something old-fashioned or obsolete
core_image: 新机器落成，旧齿轮被推到墙角落灰
scene: 新流水线刚启动，几台老机器被推进库房。 Digital printing antiquated the old press within a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 antiquate 是「使过时」（第 1 个义项：使某物变得陈旧无用）；句意为数码印刷在十年内让那台旧印刷机过时了。

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转形容词，义为「过时的；陈旧的」，是最常用形式
由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「过时；废弃」

senses.title: To make old-fashioned
senses.definition: to cause something to become outdated or no longer useful
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变得过时或不再有用
senses.example: New safety rules antiquated the factory's old wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 新的安全法规使工厂的旧线路过时了。
senses.why: The stem antiquus means 'old', and the verb ending -ate turns the adjective into an action: to give something the quality of being old.
senses.whyCN: 词干 antiquus 意为「旧的」，动词后缀 -ate 把形容词变成动作：让某物带上「旧」的性质。

senses.title: To abolish or discard as outdated
senses.definition: to put an end to a custom or practice because it belongs to the past
senses.definitionCN: 因属于过去而终止某项习俗或做法
senses.example: The council voted to antiquate the outdated toll.
senses.exampleCN: 议会投票废止了那项过时的通行费。
senses.why: Once something is stamped as old, the next step is to push it out of use entirely.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某物被贴上「旧」的标签，下一步就是把它彻底弃置不用。

intro.en: Antiquate is a Latin-style verb built on antiquus 'old', meaning literally 'to make old'.
intro.cn: antiquate 是按拉丁动词模式以 antiquus「旧的」构成的词，字面意为「使变旧」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ant- meant 'front, before'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ant- 意为「前面、在先」。

items.en: antiquus meant 'former, ancient', from ante 'before'.
items.cn: antiquus 意为「从前的、古代的」，源自 ante「在前」。

items.en: Medieval Latin antiquare meant 'to make old or obsolete'.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 antiquare 意为「使变旧、使作废」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth or seventeenth century, mostly in learned prose.
items.cn: 英语在十六至十七世纪借入这个动词，主要用于书面语。

items.en: The plain verb is now rare; its participle antiquated does nearly all the work as an adjective.
items.cn: 动词原形如今已少见；其过去分词 antiquated 作为形容词承担了几乎全部用法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the antiqu- stem; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of making things out of date.
note.cn: 形近组共享 antiqu- 词干；近义组收各种「使过时」的动词。

normal.en: antiqu- means old; -ate makes verbs like activate.

normal.en: The participle antiquated is the form you will actually meet.

normal.en: Antiquation is the abstract noun for the process.
normal.cn: antiquation 是表示这一过程的抽象名词。
